papers.title: Non-trivial invisibility fields
papers.abstract: Reducing scattering from dielectric objects is a key challenge in photonics and cloaking. Here we prove the existence of non-trivial electromagnetic field configurations - which we call invisibility fields - for which a non-trivial dielectric cylinder with a regular triangular cross-section produces…

papers.title: Determination of tripartite pure states by two overlapping marginals
papers.abstract: In many-body quantum physics, the global state encodes all correlations, but the information most naturally available is often local. This makes it important to understand when a small collection of reduced density matrices already fixes the whole state. Such uniqueness questions are especially impo…

papers.title: Spatially extended chiral states in $\mathcal{T}$-broken zero-index heterostructures
papers.abstract: Gyromagnetic zero-index media reveal an intrinsic connection between topological photonics and extreme-parameter photonics, offering the possibility of enhanced light-matter interactions. We demonstrate that the boundary branch constrained by the reflection-phase vortex at the Dirac point hybridizes…

papers.title: Resetting a Superconducting Qubit with a Compact Colder Resistive Dissipator below the Qubit Frequency
papers.abstract: Efficient qubit reset has become a key requirement for large-scale superconducting quantum processors, as initialization fidelity increasingly lags behind gate performance and quantum error correction demands rapid, high-fidelity state re-initialization. This work proposes a compact on-chip dissipator consisting of two transmon dissipation modes and a thin-film resistor, and experimentally demonstrates an unconditional reset protocol. With no additional control lines and negligible impact on the qubit $T_1$, the effective temperature of the transmon qubit is reduced from $49$~mK to $35$~mK. Quantum process tomography is employed to benchmark the reset process, achieving a process error of $0.0028$. This reset protocol is robust to pulse parameter deviations, thereby relaxing calibration requirements. The dissipator architecture provides a practical, calibration-friendly reset solution for large-scale superconducting quantum processors.

papers.title: The Structure of Shared Classical Facts in Quantum Systems
papers.abstract: Perfectly matching local outcomes need not constitute a nondisturbing shared classical record. For finite-dimensional multipartite states, we prove that nontrivial exact records are equivalent to a spectrum sharing structure with a unique finest decomposition into locally distinguishable sectors, where entanglement may persist. For a fixed complete pointer, exact sharing is equivalent to strong quantum Darwinism together with global nondisturbance, while spectrum broadcast structure additionally requires conditional independence. Arbitrarily weak full-rank admixtures eliminate exact sharing, but two-sided distance bounds quantify robustness through disturbance and disagreement, while information bounds connect accurate local readouts to observer consensus.

papers.title: Norm Bounds on Sums of Positive Operators with Applications to Monogamy Games and Quantum Key Distribution
papers.abstract: Bounding the acceptance probabilities of quantum measurements is a recurring task in quantum information theory. An acceptance probability averaged over a random measurement setting can be bounded uniformly over the input state by the operator norm of an average of positive semidefinite operators. We prove a general inequality for such norms, valid for arbitrary finite families of positive semidefinite operators and averaging distributions. We give two applications of our operator-norm inequality. First, we determine the sharp robustness threshold for the parallel BB84 monogamy-of-entanglement game. For error thresholds $β,γ\in[0,1/2]$, when the two players may make at most $βn$ and $γn$ errors, respectively, the optimal winning probability decays exponentially if $(1-2β)^2+(1-2γ)^2>1$, tends to one exponentially fast under the reverse strict inequality, and remains bounded away from zero on the boundary. Second, we establish the achievability of every asymptotic key rate $0<R<1- 2h_2(γ)$ for one-sided device-independent BB84 quantum key distribution with tolerated bit-error rate $γ$ and asymptotically optimal reconciliation, where $h_2(\cdot)$ is the binary entropy function. Alice's measurements are trusted, while Bob may perform an arbitrary joint measurement depending on the entire basis string, subject to the protocol's receipt and isolation requirements. This recovers the usual BB84 rate in this model.

papers.title: Symmetry-guided algorithms for variational quantum optimization
papers.abstract: Quantum numbers associated with symmetries classify quantum states and identify the sectors relevant to a given simulation. Generic hardware-efficient ansatzes do not necessarily preserve the quantum numbers and may therefore explore states outside the target sector. We develop symmetry-guided algorithms based on the quantum-accessible Hilbert-Schmidt asymmetry $\mathrm{A}_\mathrm{HS}$, which quantifies the deviation of a quantum state from invariance under a specified symmetry group. This quantity guides the optimization toward a highly reduced symmetry-based target sector, without enforcing the symmetry on the preparation circuit. We demonstrate the approach as a proof of principle in variational quantum eigensolver calculations targeting singlet ground states with collective SU(2) symmetry. The applications include a five-qubit $S$-wave $p+{}^3\mathrm{He}$ two-cluster Hamiltonian, deduced from $\textit{ab initio}$ many-body calculations, and collective spin models with up to 12 particles, which provide a many-particle benchmark of asymmetry-guided optimization. Across these applications, $\mathrm{A}_\mathrm{HS}$-based guidance increases the singlet probability. Overall, the proposed algorithms improve energy accuracy during optimization and ground-state fidelity compared with direct energy minimization, with substantial fidelity improvements in the larger spin systems. These results demonstrate the utility of an asymmetry objective determined by the group action, independently of the Hamiltonian energy, for improving the reliability of variational quantum optimization.

papers.title: Analytic two-body density-matrix spectrum of the Fermionic Tonks-Girardeau gas
papers.abstract: The two-body density matrix (TBDM) of a quantum many-body system provides information about particle correlations, e.g., pairing. In this work, we derive the complete spectrum of the TBDM of the fermionic Tonks-Girardeau gas using its exact ground-state wavefunction in second quantization. We obtain analytical expressions for all eigenvalues and eigenvectors for an arbitrary number of particles and identify two different types of eigenstates: collective states, formed by superpositions of paired momentum modes, and single-determinant states. We provide a physical interpretation of this structure, explaining the origin of the different eigenstates and their degeneracies. We further derive an asymptotic expansion for the largest eigenvalue, improving on previous estimates and analytically confirming its linear scaling with the particle number, thereby indicating off-diagonal long-range order. For the high-index collective states, we obtain simpler expressions for the eigenvalues and eigenvectors, showing that the eigenvalues decay as $n^{-4}$ and that the eigenvectors become independent of the number of particles. Finally, we discuss the connection between the collective states and an effective description in terms of composite bosons, whose spectral properties suggest a behavior consistent with Tan's contact for interacting bosonic systems.

papers.title: Coherence Spreading Law in Quenched Homogeneous Bose Gases
papers.abstract: We investigate nonequilibrium coherence spreading in quenched homogeneous bosonic gases both analytically and numerically. Our ensemble-averaged Gross-Pitaevskii trajectory approach and kinetic analysis confirm the linear-in-time growth of the squared coherence length, and explicitly give the spreading-law dependence on the ratio of initial energy to healing energy. When the ratio is relatively small, the squared coherence length grows at a universal rate determined by the ratio of Planck's constant to the particle mass, insensitive to interaction strength and initial momentum distributions. However, our further calculations uncover fundamental limitations to such universality and establish its phase boundaries governed by low system energies, weak interparticle interactions and many-body integrability. Our theory fully reproduces the key experimental signatures and resolves the puzzle of the dynamical origin of the recently observed universal coherence-spreading speed limit [Nature 647, 608-612 (2025)]. Going beyond existing experimental observations, we provide some testable predictions for ultracold-atom experiments and clarify the conditions for the emergence of universal coherent dynamics in nonequilibrium bosonic many-body systems.

papers.title: Exact Mirror-Parity Selection Rule for Electron-Phonon Coupling in Two-Dimensional Crystals
papers.abstract: The electron--phonon (e-ph) interaction underlies conventional superconductivity and plays a central role in transport and other many-body phenomena in solids. Here, we derive a symmetry selection rule for e-ph scattering in two-dimensional crystals possessing a horizontal mirror plane, $σ_h$. For electronic states of mirror parity $s_n(\mathbf{k})$ and $s_m(\mathbf{k}+\mathbf{q})$, and a phonon mode of parity $χ_ν(\mathbf{q})$, we show that the e-ph matrix element $g_{mn,ν}(\mathbf{k},\mathbf{q})$ vanishes identically unless $s_n(\mathbf{k})\,χ_ν(\mathbf{q})\, s_m(\mathbf{k}+\mathbf{q})=+1$. The rule follows from the covariance of the phonon-induced deformation potential under $σ_h$, constitutes the $C_s$ case of the general group-theoretical selection rule for matrix elements, and partitions the e-ph interaction throughout the Brillouin zone into symmetry-allowed and symmetry-forbidden scattering channels. Consequently, mirror-even phonons couple electronic states of the same mirror parity, either even--even or odd--odd, whereas mirror-odd phonons couple only states of opposite mirror parity, for both intra- and interband processes. We illustrate the selection rule through first-principles calculations for the two-dimensional superconductor $\mathrm{Sc_2BCH_4}$, where mirror parity is well defined throughout the entire Brillouin zone and symmetry-forbidden matrix elements vanish up to numerical precision. We then extend the analysis to bulk $\mathrm{MgB_2}$, where the rule applies exactly only on mirror-invariant planes of the three-dimensional Brillouin zone. Moving away from these planes removes the exact mirror constraint and activates scattering channels that are symmetry forbidden when the mirror eigenvalues are well defined. Our results establish horizontal mirror symmetry as an exact and practical filter of e-ph scattering processes.

papers.title: Efficient training of a 128-modes 3D continuously coupled photonic chip via limited quantum resources
papers.abstract: Integrated photonics provides a promising route towards the development of large-scale, stable and low-loss quantum hardware. Existing implementations of universal quantum photonic chips generally rely on architectures consisting of localised interactions between the modes that can be programmed with known algorithms to implement specific operations. Recent advances have shown that interferometers based on 3D continuously coupled waveguide arrays may allow to significantly scale up the number of modes with reduced overhead. However, for this class of devices, optimal strategies to set the controllable parameters and obtain the desired transformation have not been demonstrated generally. In this work, we report the use of a machine learning algorithm driven by quantum data to program the operation of a reconfigurable three-dimensional continuously coupled photonic device comprising 128 modes. We show experimentally the capability of reaching a target unitary matrix, among those achievable by the device, through a limited number of one- and two-photon measurements. Our results demonstrate that this approach results to be effective in the presence of noise and with a limited amount of resources, also allowing to partially compensate imperfections in the experimental setup. This method can thus represent a viable route towards programming large scale integrated photonic devices, unlocking the possibility of controlling photonic systems for which an analytical decomposition is not trivial.

papers.title: Quantum error correcting codes from quiver moduli: Grassmannians, cyclic monodromy, and argyle collision divisors
papers.abstract: Building on aspects of a recent diagrammatic field-theory programme for quantum error correction put forward by the first-named author (arXiv:2607.08911), we construct exact finite-dimensional codes from twisted cyclic and argyle quiver moduli on the projective line. A regular fibre of the node-labelled cyclic Hitchin map records the ways to distribute simple spectral zeroes among the arrows with prescribed degrees. The Hilbert space spanned by these allocations is a Young permutation module. Root monodromy acts on its Specht factors and leaves their multiplicity spaces noiseless. Resetting the Specht factor therefore recovers the encoded state for every channel in the monodromy noise model. We prove that the largest Kostka multiplicity is the optimal dimension of a subspace code correcting the full monodromy algebra, even among codes spanning several isotypic blocks. Quantizing an argyle master space recovers the cyclic sheet space as a weight sector of a tensor power, with the identification preserving monodromy. For the balanced three-cycle with $t$ zeroes per arrow, the multiplicity of a partition $(a,b,c)$ of $3t$ is $1+\min(a-b,b-c)$. The optimal logical dimension is thus $t+1$, attained uniquely by the block indexed by $(2t,t)$. At $t=1$ we give explicit codewords for a qubit on six sheets. The commuting right action generates its full logical algebra, yielding errors outside the monodromy model that leave the measured footprint statistics unchanged yet require different recoveries. We also compute collision-parity ranks, give a higher-rank Grassmannian example, and derive a conditional criterion for recovery across splitting types.

papers.title: From Claws to Conferences: Device-Independent Key Agreement Beyond Non-Signaling
papers.abstract: Device-independent conference key agreement (DI-CKA) allows a group of users to establish a common secret key without trusting the internal operation of their quantum devices. Existing DI-CKA protocols derive their security from multipartite Bell tests and therefore require the device components not to communicate during each round. We present, to the best of our knowledge, the first DI-CKA protocol that removes this non-signaling assumption: all interfaces and their mutual communication are treated as one untrusted device, which only has to be quantum polynomial-time while the protocol runs. Assuming that the Learning With Errors (LWE) problem is hard for quantum algorithms with quantum advice during the execution, we prove finite-size security against coherent attacks, in which the device may keep quantum memory and correlate and adapt its behavior across rounds. For two parties the protocol is a computational DI-QKD protocol with an explicit finite-size proof against coherent attacks. Technically, we lift the claw state underlying the classical-verifier test of Brakerski et al.\ (FOCS 2018) to multipartite entanglement, obtaining a \emph{GHZ-correlated claw state}. %that is prepared with one coherent claw-free function evaluation and $N-1$ CNOT gates. We then introduce the \emph{collective adaptive hardcore bit}, a multiparty generalization of the adaptive hardcore bit of Brakerski et al.\ and show that it follows from the original property by a tight reduction. Combined with Jordan's lemma, an entropic uncertainty relation, and entropy accumulation, this certifies smooth min-entropy of the key against an external quantum adversary. Our protocol achieves \emph{everlasting security}: LWE needs to hold only during the execution, because the final key is statistically secure and its secrecy persists even if LWE is broken after the protocol ends.

papers.title: Raychaudhuri-Ehlers Kinematics on Quantum State-Space: Caustics and Extrinsic Quantum Geometry
papers.abstract: Quantum mechanics is inherently geometric in that the pure states form a curved complex manifold and the Schrödinger evolution defines a Hamiltonian flow on this space. Geometry identifies constraints on flows on quantum state-space that hold independently of their microscopic realization. We uncover such universal behavior in families of geodesic paths on the quantum state-space using the Raychaudhuri-Ehlers equations. We show that the complex structure leads to tidal anisotropy in the curvature, and for Hilbert space dimension $N\geq3$, complete point-emitted geodesic bundles necessarily develop shear and undergo direction-selective focusing at finite distance. We give these geometric results an information-theoretic interpretation in terms of fidelity susceptibility and quantum Fisher information. For ground-state manifolds constrained by physical parameters, we resolve the tidal curvature into Berry-curvature-dependent ambient tides and contributions from extrinsic bending within the full ambient state space. We further relate extrinsic bending to variations in the unitary generator of motion along intrinsic geodesics. We present exact many-body geometric results for the transverse-field XY spin chain. The product structure of the ground state leads to an exact cancellation of the ambient tide, including its Berry-curvature enhancement, by extrinsic curvature contributions. At the zero-field Ising point, we obtain exact results at finite size and show that the shear source for anisotropy-directed motion is entirely extrinsic relative to the full many-body state-space. For the metric in the thermodynamic limit, the geodesic families exhibit repeated $A_2$ fold catastrophes inside the ferromagnetic phase. Our framework thus separates universal state-space effects from those of physical restrictions and exposes their consequences in a paradigmatic many-body system.

papers.title: Quantum computing for high energy nuclear physics
papers.abstract: Quantum information science (QIS) offers a new set of conceptual and computational tools ideally suited to exploring the many-body, out-of-equilibrium, and real-time properties of strongly interacting quantum systems. These themes find a natural counterpart in high energy nuclear physics, whose central goal is to describe the properties of Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD), the theory of the strong interaction, under extreme conditions. Relevant examples range from the formation and internal structure of hadrons, to the collective and thermalization dynamics of strongly interacting QCD matter, and the properties of complex many-body scattering processes. Although tremendous progress has been made over the past decades in our understanding of QCD in the nuclear physics context, through perturbative methods, lattice QCD, and effective theory descriptions, phenomena that are intrinsically connected to real-time dynamics, highly entangled many-body evolution, or finite density regimes remain only partially accessible with existing approaches. In this article, we argue that QIS can help realize a new paradigm for addressing these open questions. With the aim of making the discussion accessible to both high energy nuclear physics and QIS audiences, we provide an overview of selected open problems in high energy nuclear physics, with emphasis on aspects motivated by collider phenomenology, and discuss how they can be approached using QIS tools. This connection is illustrated through representative examples drawn from the recent literature, making the case that QIS can become a driving force for discovery in nuclear physics in the coming years.

papers.title: Dynamically modulated light-matter interactions for ancilla-tolerant bosonic control
papers.abstract: Strong light-matter interactions are central to state-of-the-art quantum technologies, spanning platforms as diverse as Rydberg atoms, trapped ions, and superconducting circuits. In superconducting circuits, the strong dispersive coupling between microwave photons (light) and ancillary qubits (matter) has enabled universal bosonic control and quantum error correction. However, this always-on dispersive interaction propagates errors from the ancillary qubits to the bosonic systems both while idling and when performing operations, introducing a trade-off between control strength and fidelity. We break this trade-off by introducing a parametrically activated hybridization between the bosonic modes and ancilla qubits, keeping both elements decoupled when not active. When activated, this hybridization mediates a dynamic light-matter coupling with non-trivial engineered symmetries, permitting resilience to ancilla decay and dephasing. This dynamic coupling functions as a new control primitive that offers a route to bosonic processors whose performance is set by the oscillator, rather than the ancilla.

papers.title: Universal dynamics of quantum phase transitions with fractional long-range interactions
papers.abstract: The complete statistical characterization of defects generated in a quantum phase transition has mostly been studied in exactly solvable models, and remains little explored in nonintegrable systems such as long-range interacting spin chains. We characterize the full defect counting statistics in a nonintegrable long-range spin chain, the fractional Ising model, by time-dependent variational-principle simulations within the matrix-product-state and matrix-product-operator formalism. Fractional interactions capture emergent multiscale correlations and long-range effects in nature, governed by the order of the underlying fractional derivative. Such couplings can be approximated on existing quantum simulation platforms, where the full defect statistics can be measured. The defect number cumulants follow power laws in the driving time, with exponents that vary continuously with the fractional order. At low fractional order, deep in the long-range regime, the mean defect number decays more slowly than predicted by the Kibble-Zurek mechanism (KZM), while at intermediate order the KZM holds with the numerically extracted many-body critical exponents. At large fractional order, the exactly solvable free-fermion limit of the model becomes progressively more accurate towards the short-range limit. We derive exact bounds on the kink-number cumulants and on the kink-kink correlations, implying an exact Gaussian limiting distribution for large system sizes. In the many-body simulations, however, kinks are more correlated, consistent with the confinement of domain walls, and these bounds are violated in the long-range regime, also in the bulk of the chain. Nevertheless, the kink distribution still approaches a Gaussian for large defect numbers, with proportionality partially broken between the cumulants.

papers.title: DynaMite: Dynamic Measurement Scheduling To Accelerate Fault-Tolerant Quantum Programs
papers.abstract: Fault-tolerant quantum computers run millions of logical cycles to perform quantum error correction (QEC). As logical operations span entire logical cycles, the logical cycle time (LCT) dictates program runtime. Qubit measurements, critical to extract parity information for QEC, are the slowest operations and account for 43-86% of LCT. Measurement latencies impact fidelity: fast measurements lower our ability to correctly classify quantum states, whereas slow measurements increase the likelihood of decoherence. Hardware providers thus calibrate measurement latencies that maximize readout fidelity per qubit and use them to schedule all measurements during program execution. However, calibrated latencies are sub-optimal for logical performance because logical cycles span multiple QEC rounds, during which data qubits are not measured. This increases LCT and logical error rates (LERs) due to decoherence at the logical level. We propose DynaMite, a lightweight real-time measurement latency selection policy built on two key insights. First, logical cycles must use a measurement latency that is fast enough to reduce both LCT and LER for the QEC code, instead of the calibrated latency that only maximizes readout fidelity. Second, not all logical cycles are equal; many do not fully utilize the error budget of the QEC code, i.e., the number of failed parity checks it can tolerate without compromising LER. These cycles could use even faster measurements but do not, because latencies are chosen statically, whereas error information is only available at runtime. DynaMite exploits the fact that a logical cycle comprises multiple QEC rounds and selects the fastest latency for an upcoming round based on the error budget left and rounds remaining. Our evaluations show that DynaMite reduces LCT by 1.69x on average and up to 2.29x, and reduces LER to 0.46x on average and up to 0.13x of baseline.

papers.title: Two examples in amplituhedron tilings
papers.abstract: We give an example of a tiling of the $m=4$ amplituhedron that has fewer cells than that of the magic number conjecture. The tiling uses an injective degree two cell.

papers.title: Data informed Ansatz Selection for Variational Quantum Circuits
papers.abstract: Choosing a variational quantum circuit (VQC) usually means searching over ansatze and depths, and training each candidate. We give three rules that fix these choices from the data and the gate set alone, before any training. First, a circuit without entangling gates has a rank-one Fourier coefficient tensor on every subset of qubits. A singular value decomposition of a dataset's Fourier coefficients therefore indicates whether entanglement is needed, which qubits it connects, and a lower bound on the error of omitting it. Second, the rank of the quantum Fisher information matrix grows by $p_0$ per layer, after a first-layer deficit $d_0$, until it reaches a ceiling set by the dynamical Lie algebra. This law fixes the depth. Third, reading out all $2^N - 1$ Pauli-Z products from one batch of shots resolves half of the state's directions, the most any single-basis readout can. A single-qubit readout resolves an exponentially small fraction. For the Madelon dataset, the rules prescribe 7 blocks of 3 qubits at depth 3: a 239-parameter classifier with 78.5% test accuracy, found without a grid search. Ablations confirm three predicted effects: shallower circuits, smaller blocks and dropping reuploading all lower accuracy.

papers.title: The integer spectrum of a superintegrable quantum field theory
papers.abstract: In our previous article CMP 407 (2026) 131, we explored the rich algebraic structures arising from a specific quantum many-body Hamiltonian quartic in the bosonic creation-annihilation operators. This Hamiltonian originated from the works of Gérard and Grellier on classical turbulent energy transfer in a Lax-integrable setting, and its quantum version respects hierarchies of polynomial conservation laws all of which possess purely integer spectra, as does the Hamiltonian itself. The latter feature, known from numerical studies, has previously remained unproved. Here, we present an elementary solution of the quantum Gérard-Grellier Hamiltonian. The eigenstates are labelled by partitions and the corresponding eigenvalues admit simple explicit expressions in terms of the principal hook lengths. The key ingredient in this construction is a specific basis we introduce, inspired by the classical multisoliton coherent states, in which the Hamiltonian is upper-triangular. The expressions for the eigenvalues then immediately follow, while the full eigenbasis can be recovered via a Gram-Schmidt procedure.

papers.title: Synchronization Mpemba Effect
papers.abstract: We introduce the synchronization Mpemba effect, in which a less synchronized initial state overtakes a more synchronized one, and demonstrate it in dissipatively coupled quantum van der Pol oscillators. Within a graph-Laplacian framework, we show that for two oscillators, the mechanism is a competition between a slowly decaying collective background and a fast transverse transient, equivalently an exchange between relative-mode displacement and phase-fluctuation errors. The same decomposition extends to networks: the synchronization error splits into transverse Laplacian modes, yielding closed-form crossing times from eigenvalue separations and initial mode weights, and a sufficient screening criterion. With only these eigenvalues entering, the rule is topology independent: crossing times of different networks collapse onto a single spectral-gap line. Thus, quantum many-body dynamics can be designed and controlled at low dimension without constructing the exponentially large Liouvillian, opening a route to quantum synchronization as a resource.

papers.title: Band structure of two-dimensional graphene and of one-dimensional nanoribbons via variational quantum algorithms: from energies to wavefunction quality
papers.abstract: Simulating quantum many-body systems classically encounters exponential bottlenecks, which quantum devices circumvent by natively encoding wavefunctions. In the Noisy Intermediate-Scale Quantum (NISQ) era, however, hardware noise constrains simulation accuracy. As a stepping stone toward strongly correlated materials, we compute the band structure of 2D monolayer graphene and 1D nanoribbons (zigzag and armchair) using a single variational workflow in the $p_z$ tight-binding approximation. Non-interacting ground states also provide essential initial reference states for subspace and warm-started variational methods to solve interacting spectra. By mapping the Bloch Hamiltonian to Pauli operators, we extract the ground band via the Variational Quantum Eigensolver (VQE) and excited subbands via Variational Quantum Deflation (VQD), validating our approach from ideal simulations to execution on physical IBM Quantum processors. In ideal simulations, the workflow reproduces exact diagonalization results with high precision, whereas hardware noise introduces energy deviations of a few hundredths of the hopping parameter. While qubit counts scale logarithmically with ribbon width, fixed-depth ansatz accuracy degrades with Hilbert space dimension. Crucially, deepening the ansatz improves ideal simulation accuracy by over three orders of magnitude but worsens energy estimates under noise, proving that practical circuit depth is bounded by hardware noise rather than expressivity. Finally, we complement energy evaluations with a wavefunction-level diagnostic measuring subspace containment. This diagnostic captures degenerate manifolds and exposes optimization failure modes disguised by energy agreement alone. Operating directly on NISQ hardware, this validated workflow establishes a controlled baseline for studying topological and strongly correlated phases in realistic materials.

papers.title: Generalized Lorentz Framework for Active Semiconductor Quantum Surface Plasmonics
papers.abstract: Nanostructured semiconductors provide an actively tunable platform for light-matter interactions across a broad spectral range. As feature sizes shrink to the deep nanoscale (~10 nm scale), nonclassical carrier dynamics and surface plasmonic responses become prominent, creating substantial challenges for a rigorous and efficient theoretical treatment. Here we develop a generalized Lorentz framework for quantum surface plasmonics in nanostructured semiconductors with arbitrary energymomentum dispersion relations. The framework enables efficient quantitative treatment of carrier nonlocality, carrier surface accumulation and depletion, and nonlocal damping in three-dimensional semiconductor nanostructures, under electrical tuning and across a wide range of doping densities. Building on this framework, we further establish a rigorous quasinormal-mode analysis that provides transparent physical insight into complex surface plasmonic responses of multiscale semiconductor structures. We demonstrate electrically controlled deep-nanoscale carrier accumulation and depletion in a semiconductor nanoantenna, leading to pronounced plasmonic-response modulation that can be interpreted in terms of eigenmode shifts, creation, and annihilation. By quantifying and linking complex nonclassical carrier dynamics with plasmonic eigenmodes, our work establishes a comprehensive quantitative framework for active semiconductor quantum surface plasmonics and will foster the convergence of electronics and photonics at the deep nanoscale.

papers.title: Autonomous cooling of Kerr-cat qubits to minutes-long bit-flip times
papers.abstract: Quantum error correction becomes more hardware efficient when physical noise is strongly biased towards one error channel. Cat qubits realize such a bias by encoding information in two opposite coherent states of a superconducting oscillator, so that bit flips are exponentially suppressed with photon number while phase-flip rates increase only linearly. In Kerr-cat qubits, a driven double-well potential confines these states and enables fast coherent control, but excitations can induce interwell switching, limiting bit-flip times to milliseconds. Here we show that the nonlinear interaction generating the confinement can also cool these excitations. When an intra-well transition becomes resonant with a lossy readout mode, excitations are transferred out of the qubit and dissipated, as established by spectroscopy and relaxation measurements. We observe the predicted exponential scaling of Kerr-cat bit-flip times with photon number, reaching 450 s, over five orders of magnitude beyond previous demonstrations. Phase-flip rates remain consistent with intrinsic photon loss at operating points with seconds-long bit-flip times. We further demonstrate fast Z gates without measurable degradation of bit-flip protection and single-shot readout with a bit-flip probability below $10^{-6}$ per measurement. Autonomous cooling thus brings minutes-long bit-flip protection to Kerr-cat qubits while retaining fast coherent control, without additional cooling drives or circuit elements.

papers.title: Weakly viscous nonlocal wave equations: forward theory, Lebesgue Runge approximation, and inverse problems
papers.abstract: We study forward and inverse problems for weakly viscous nonlocal wave equations with elastic term $(-Δ)^s u$ and dissipative term $(-Δ)^r\partial_tu$, where $0\leq r<s$. For time-dependent potentials in suitable $L^\infty(0,T;L^p(Ω))$ classes, we establish finite energy well-posedness, strong continuity in time, and an energy identity by parabolic regularization and time-regularization arguments. Under explicit nonlocality and nonresonance assumptions on the fractional orders, we prove Runge approximation in $L^2(0,T;\widetilde H^r(Ω))$ and hence in $L^2(Ω\times(0,T))$. As an application, partial exterior Dirichlet-to-Neumann measurements uniquely determine the potential in all three exponent regimes of the Runge theorem, including integer elastic orders with noninteger dissipative orders. The recovery argument combines equality of solutions with the same exterior input, unique continuation or the entanglement principle, and a single Lebesgue-space Runge approximation. It applies to the full admissible potential class, without spatial boundedness, sign, or smallness assumptions.

papers.title: Bulk and edge states in Fibonacci-Bose-Hubbard clusters
papers.abstract: We study the one- and two-boson energy subspaces of finite open Bose--Hubbard chains with Fibonacci-modulated hopping and zero on-site potential. Their spectra exhibit a hierarchy of bands and gaps, and a critical zero-energy mode for odd lengths, in agreement with prior research. For the singe-excitation subspace we find two families of length-invariant finite-energy states localized at the left cluster boundary. For the two-boson subspace, we report both doublon and separated-pair excitations in the form of Tamm/Shockley states localized near either end. In particular, the right-edge doublon states occur across all Fibonacci generations whereas the left-side states appear every second generation. We check numerically that the second-order perturbation theory accounts well for the structure of the spectrum and the edge states in the doublon subspace in the strong-coupling regime. The results are useful for future explorations of many-body physics beyond numerical tractability, specifically using near-term Josephson quantum simulators.

papers.title: Closed- and open-system characterization of the Yukawa-SYK model in real time
papers.abstract: Strongly correlated matter without quasiparticles is central to many-body physics, quantum chaos, and quantum gravity, motivating a considerable effort toward its realization in tabletop experiments. Two challenges remain: laboratory platforms are open systems, so conformal behavior must survive dissipation, and it must be identified through measurable quantities. We address both challenges in the Yukawa-Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev (YSYK) model, in which bosons and fermions interact as in, e.g., light-matter systems, but through random all-to-all couplings that drive the boson to criticality without fine tuning. Solving the model in real time using the Schwinger-Keldysh formalism, we treat closed and open systems within a unified framework and, in both cases, consider a thermal steady state to map their phase diagrams. In addition to the known conformal and impurity (or SYK$_2$) regimes, we identify novel high-temperature regimes in which the fermions are driven by an essentially bare boson and show that their dynamics is captured by a quadratic model with time-dependent random hopping. Across all regimes, the fermionic softening of the boson is bounded by a ``criticality budget'' determined only by the Yukawa coupling and the temperature. Coupling the boson with a thermal environment induces a mass shift that deforms the boundaries between different regimes and exhausts the criticality budget, thus imposing a bound on temperature and dissipation rate compatible with self-tuned criticality. We further introduce a set of markers built from the two-point functions that separate all identified regimes, are accessible in linear response, and require no fit of the conformal exponents. We complement them with the quantum Fisher information, deriving upper bounds with and without dissipation. These results may help characterize holographic quantum matter beyond the closed setting.

papers.title: Quantum Simulation of Electronic Structure using Quantum Density Functional Theory on a Programmable Integrated Photonic Circuit
papers.abstract: Quantum simulations of molecular electronic structure hold the potential for computational advantage but are inherently limited by the linear scaling of qubit requirements with respect to system size. Quantum Density Functional Theory (Q-DFT) addresses this constraint by reformulating the interacting many-body problem in terms of a non-interacting Kohn--Sham reference system. Here, we present and experimentally validate a Q-DFT algorithm that requires only $\mathcal{O}(\log_2(N))$ qubits to simulate a system of $N$ orbitals, thereby reducing resource overhead. More precisely, we solve the Kohn--Sham problem for the lithium hydride (LiH) molecule using the ensemble extension of the variational quantum eigensolver paradigm that minimizes the energy of the system in the subspace spanned by the ground and first excited states. To execute this task, we encode the problem with qubits on a quantum photonic platform, utilizing an architecture that combines a deterministic quantum dot single-photon source with a programmable integrated photonic circuit. By evaluating the molecular ground- and first excited-state properties, this work establishes a pathway for simulating larger molecular systems, demonstrating the viability of integrating qubit-efficient algorithms with advanced reconfigurable photonic hardware for near-term quantum chemistry applications.

papers.title: Universal quantum gate set for multimode Schrödinger cat states stabilized by nonlocal dissipation engineering
papers.abstract: Schrödinger cat states provide a hardware-efficient platform for bosonic quantum error correction by encoding logical information in protected manifolds of harmonic oscillators. While previous work has demonstrated the dissipative stabilization of multi-mode Schrödinger cat states as robust quantum …

papers.abstract: Dissipation, though often detrimental to quantum entanglement, can be manipulated for the preparation of entangled states, wherein ingeniously designed quantum jump processes drive the system toward the desired steady state. Here we venture beyond this paradigm, and demonstrate a new type of entangl…

papers.abstract: Four-fermion interactions appear in effective descriptions of particle physics, many-body systems, and gravitational theories with fermions. Although the same local operator may enter perturbative scattering, a vacuum Nambu–Jona-Lasinio (NJL) instability, or finite-density Bardeen-Cooper-Schrieffer …

papers.title: Dynamical aspects of steady-state subradiance: Detailed balance and its breakdown
papers.abstract: The dynamics of dissipative many-body quantum systems sometimes admit an emergent classical description in terms of a Markov chain even though the corresponding state space contains highly entangled states. In particular, a bad-cavity laser is a paradigm system whose dynamics can be formulated as a …

papers.title: Wigner-Function Fingerprints of Collective Excitations in Mirror-Terminated Waveguide QED
papers.abstract: We investigate the emission profiles of singly excited collective states and propose a matched-mode witnessing protocol in a mirror-terminated waveguide quantum electrodynamics system. The amplitudes and relative phases of the initial collective excitation are encoded in the temporal mode of the emitted single-photon wavepacket, providing a route to state verification through the common waveguide output. We identify the emission mode associated with a chosen target state and employ an auxiliary virtual-cavity representation to evaluate the quantum state of this selected output mode. For a matched initial state, the selected mode contains the emitted single photon, whose Wigner function exhibits a pronounced non-classical negative dip, serving as a distinct fingerprint of the target many-body state. With the reference mode held fixed, different initial configurations yield different photon occupations and phase-space distributions, demonstrating the state selectivity of the protocol. These results connect collective-state verification with temporal-mode analysis of the emitted radiation, offering access to collective coherence with reduced reliance on qubit-resolved correlation measurements.

papers.title: Reasoning about Shared-Qubit Concurrency in Quantum Computing
papers.abstract: In this paper, we develop a semantic model for the parallel execution of quantum circuits, providing a formal foundation for studying shared-qubit concurrency in quantum computing. As in classical shared-memory concurrency, parallel quantum circuits may interfere with one another through operations on shared qubits. However, quantum entanglement and the noncommutativity of quantum operations introduce additional challenges for reasoning about their correctness. To address these challenges, we generalise the classical Owicki-Gries method to quantum computing at the level of quantum circuits. Our approach enables compositional reasoning about parallel quantum circuits by separating the verification of individual components from the analysis of interference between them. We formulate proof rules for establishing the correctness of parallel quantum circuits and prove their soundness with respect to the proposed semantic model.

papers.title: Initialization-controlled fault sensitivity and force-balance plateaus in noisy variational quantum optimization
papers.abstract: We study deep variational circuits for a periodic Heisenberg chain under local gate depolarization, at depths where noiseless training is coherently exact. Full-width initializations reach low coherent error faster than circuits with confined transverse generators, but incur a larger noise shift and need an order of magnitude more updates for noisy convergence. In many-body-localization-inspired initialization, bounding the initial transverse generator amplitudes keeps the operator support localized and suffices for low-fragility optimization, so longitudinal disorder and Floquet layer repetition are unnecessary. The fault-erasure fraction, the mean fraction of coherent energy removed per fault, sets the effective visibility through a parameter-free exponential model. Full-width circuits start with delocalized operator support, and once coherent energy builds up, each fault erases nearly all of it. Initially, their noise-induced gradient almost uniformly attenuates the coherent gradient, so coherent descent proceeds at the noiseless rate. They then stall on a high-noise force-balance plateau, where finite coherent and noise-induced gradients cancel to first order. At late times all initializations reach the same fault-erasure fraction and noisy-error band, but operator support contracts more slowly, at a rate set by the plateau residence time.

papers.title: Gaussian Quantum Integrated Sensing and Communication
papers.abstract: We consider a quantum integrated sensing and communication problem over an optical link in which a low-power transmitter simultaneously communicates with a receiver and identifies the range of a defect producing a backscattered signal. We model the system as a lossy thermal-noise bosonic channel, in which the target, modeled as a beamsplitter, affects the timing of the backscattered signal through its location. Motivated by the envisioned deployment of entanglement-enabled quantum networks, we develop two protocols that allow the transmitter to leverage shared Gaussian entanglement, in the form of independent two-mode squeezed vacuum states or coupled three-mode squeezed vacuum states, to assist both sensing and communication. Since entanglement is known to enhance sensing, as demonstrated in quantum illumination, and to increase communication rates through entanglement-assisted communication, the transmitter faces a trade-off in allocating its entanglement resources between the two tasks. Our main results characterize these trade-offs under the proposed protocols in terms of achievable communication rate/sensing error-exponent regions, which outperform time-sharing schemes and demonstrate a quantum advantage.

papers.title: Pump quantization changes optimal measurements for quantum sensing
papers.abstract: Standard analyses of quantum phase sensing often neglect the overhead of generating squeezed-light by treating the pump as an undepleted classical resource. Realistically, the pump is a quantum object that undergoes significant depletion and entangles with the produced squeezed light, raising the question of how the crossover from a classical to a quantum pump limits the quantum advantage in sensing. Contrary to prior analyses, we show that quantum advantage persists despite pump quantization, but depends critically on the nonlinear $(χ^{(2)})$ source dynamics. In particular, we demonstrate that Heisenberg scaling emerges in the regime of strong pump depletion, rather than maximum signal squeezing. At maximum squeezing, the quantum Fisher information (QFI) for interferometric sensing of an unknown phase scales as $N^{3/2}$, where $N$ is the pump photon number, surpassing the shot-noise limit but establishing that squeezing itself is insufficient to attain Heisenberg scaling of $N^2$. At maximal pump depletion, where the signal flux is maximized, the QFI scales as $N^2$. In this regime, standard photon counting is suboptimal, while a joint nonlinear measurement of the entire pump-signal system is shown to achieve Heisenberg scaling. Our work shows that pump quantization changes both the optimal operating point and the measurement strategies required to preserve a realistic quantum advantage in phase estimation and, more broadly, many-body quantum dynamics.

papers.title: Liouvillian Kramers Degeneracy
papers.abstract: The Kramers theorem generally guarantees the spectral degeneracy of time-reversal-invariant Hamiltonian operators with half-integer spin, underlying a variety of physical phenomena. Despite its fundamental significance, the Kramers degeneracy has been argued to be absent in Liouvillian superoperators acting on mixed states because of the double structure of the Hilbert space. Here, we instead demonstrate that the interplay of time-reversal symmetry$^†$ and parity symmetry enforces the Kramers degeneracy in Liouvillians. We explicitly construct dissipative many-body models of interacting fermions and spins exhibiting the Kramers degeneracy and show that their complex spectral statistics follow those of non-Hermitian random matrices in the corresponding symplectic symmetry classes. Of the three fundamental universality classes of non-Hermitian random matrices, the symplectic class has never been realized in symmetry-resolved many-body Liouvillians. Our constructions provide its explicit realizations and spectral signatures of nonintegrability in symplectic open quantum systems.

papers.title: Reconstruction of the conformal algebra from a critical groundstate on the (fuzzy) sphere
papers.abstract: Recently, we found a method to reconstruct the dilatation operator (sphere Hamiltonian) from a regulated conformal field theory groundstate. In this paper, we explore methods to construct the whole global conformal algebra, and test our construction using fuzzy sphere regularization. Starting from a groundstate of the same Hamiltonian, these methods perform better than constructions of the conformal generators based on a Hamiltonian density, are model-independent, require no additional tuning, and improve with system size. One purpose of reconstructing the conformal algebra is to identify conformal primary states, which we do with some success. We also find further evidence supporting the model of the short-distance corrections to the entanglement Hamiltonian proposed earlier and use it to make systematic improvements.

papers.title: Long-range entangled criticality from coherent errors
papers.abstract: We find that coherent error can induce a phase transition from the clean surface code phase into an extended long-range entangled critical regime with diverging Markov length. To demonstrate this, we establish two general results of independent interest. The first relates topology and quantum information to mixed-state entanglement: we show that when a noise channel acting on a topological code preserves a higher-form symmetry and nonzero coherent information, the noisy state for generic logical input is long-range entangled. The second generalizes the local recovery construction based on finite Markov length to any locally parameterized family, thus encompassing local Lindbladian evolution, coherent errors followed by syndrome dephasing, and thermal states. We apply these results to the honeycomb surface code, in which we find an extended long-range entangled critical regime that is a quasi-long-ranged counterpart of 1-form strong-to-weak spontaneous symmetry breaking. As a byproduct of these studies, we relate the conditional mutual information to conductance in a Majorana network model.

papers.title: Optimised finite key for satellite up-link entangled quantum key distribution
papers.abstract: Entanglement-based quantum key distribution from ground to satellite has been proposed as a scalable primitive for global quantum networks and will be demonstrated as part of the imminent QEYSSat mission. Both theoretical studies and experimental emulations have shown that a significant asymptotic key rate can be expected. In this work we investigate this scenario with a more rigorous security analysis taking into account the finite size effects that arise from short block lengths common in satellite transmission. Our findings suggest a slight alteration of the optimal source operation when informed by finite statistics as opposed to the asymptotic regime, notably that the pump power should be slightly lowered. We quantify the annual key rate based on a dynamically optimised source operation for the Heriot-Watt ground station and several satellite parameters. We find an improved annual key rate when accumulating all raw key material before extracting a secure key instead of doing so for each overpass. We ultimately show that QEYSSat will be able to generate a significant secure annual key with both strategies.

papers.title: Studentized inference in randomized experiments when a few units dominate the outcome variation
papers.abstract: In completely randomized experiments with heavy-tailed outcomes, a few units can carry a share of the residual variation that does not vanish as the number of units grows. We study the studentized difference in means and Lin's regression-adjusted estimator, with covariates whose leverage vanishes, when the finite population is fixed, and the treatment assignment is the only source of randomness. The studentized statistic then has a nonnormal limit in general. Populations with the same marginal distributions of potential outcomes can have different limits, as the limit depends on the unobserved pairing mechanism of the two potential outcomes of each dominant unit. When the outcome errors are drawn from a heavy-tailed law, the limit is random and, outside a degenerate case, varies with the population. Under balanced allocation, the conventional Wald interval has an explicit asymptotic coverage floor. At the nominal level $0.95$, the floor is about $0.42$ for every population and about $0.84$ when the two potential residuals of each unit are equal. Both floors are close to the best possible, and without balanced allocation, the coverage can fall to the smaller of the proportions of treated and control units.

papers.title: On the Failure Probability of Quantum Leftover Hashing with Bad Seeds
papers.abstract: We study hashing against quantum adversaries, as used in cryptographic applications, and provide bounds on the probability of failure in practical settings where seeds might be reused and might be non-ideal. Randomness extraction and privacy amplification are key components of quantum cryptographic protocols, such as quantum randomness generation or key distribution, that allow the compression of partially secure raw data into shorter output with high security. To ensure the security of any cryptographic construction that integrates them, it is desirable to establish composable security. This can be done by using methods based on universal hashing and leveraging the general leftover hash lemma, which allows extraction of near-uniform random numbers from an imperfect entropy source by sampling from an almost two-universal family of hash functions using a seed. This approach is taken in many practical implementations, commonly using Toeplitz hashing. The lemma provides an upper bound $\varepsilon$ on the distance of the output to uniform randomness, which holds on average over the choice of seeds. It makes no claim that any particular seed yields near-uniform random numbers. This poses a problem for practical applications where a seed is sampled once and reused for many rounds (blockwise hashing). Here, we study the subset of \textit{bad} seeds yielding far-from-uniform outputs. We show that randomness extraction against quantum side information is guaranteed to produce $δ$-close-to-uniform random numbers except with failure probability $\left(\frac{\varepsilon}δ\right)^2$. This result is generalised to blockwise hashing providing a guarantee of the security of $k$ rounds except with failure probability $\big(\frac{(2k-1)\varepsilon}δ\big)^2$. Moreover, we extend the general leftover hash lemma to blockwise hashing and relax the assumption of almost two-universality.

papers.title: Exceptional Points and Optimized Encoding in Qubit Stabilizer Codes
papers.abstract: Continuous blind stabilizer measurements turn stabilizer codes into a Liouvillian spectral problem in which Hamiltonian terms compete with dissipative error channels. We show that this competition generically enables Liouvillian exceptional points, whose occurrence at weak error rates is constrained by the code distance. Exceptional points are detrimental in this regime of error correction as they maximize the decay rate of encoded coherences. We then optimize the encoding of the logical qubit using the eigenmodes of the Lindblad operator. This phase-optimized encoding cancels the linear short-time decay of logical qubit coherences. We apply this encoding to the [[5,1,3]] code and demonstrate that it outperforms naive encoding methods near the exceptional point, improves the fidelity of a logical $π$ rotation and remains effective in the presence of additional weak error channels.

papers.title: Lossless propagation bounds for long-range fermionic interactions
papers.abstract: We prove propagation estimates for extensive fermionic many-body interactions with polynomial time growth, no loss of spatial decay, and an optimal threshold for the polynomial spatial exponent. More precisely, we construct local representatives of evolved fermionic many-body interactions on metric spaces with polynomial volume growth of order $d_{\mathrm{vol}}$ and suitable cell partitions. For the even Hamiltonian interaction $Φ_u$ and the even interaction $Ψ$ being evolved, we assume bounds, uniform in the site, on sums of term norms over finite supports $X$ containing a given site, with weights $e^{κ|X|}(1+\operatorname{diam}X)^a$ and $e^{κ|X|}(1+\operatorname{diam}X)^p$, respectively. Here $a>d_{\mathrm{vol}}$, $0\le p\le a$, $κ$ is sufficiently large, and the Hamiltonian bound is uniform in time. We construct local representatives whose interaction norms with weight $e^{c(1+|t-s|)^{-b}|X|}(1+\operatorname{diam}X)^p$ grow at most polynomially in $|t-s|$, for suitable $c,b>0$. In particular, $p=a$ is allowed: the Hamiltonian need not decay faster than the interaction being evolved. The threshold $a>d_{\mathrm{vol}}$ is optimal in general: uniform polynomial time bounds at $p=a$ fail for $0<a\le d_{\mathrm{vol}}$, even for smooth time-dependent two-site interactions. Polynomial time growth permits integration against filters with sufficiently many finite absolute moments, including those used in quasi-adiabatic constructions and quantum belief propagation. We derive consequences for filtered interactions and the dynamics they generate, providing dynamical estimates for perturbation theory with extensive perturbations, including gap stability, the principle that local perturbations perturb locally (LPPL), adiabatic theory, and response theory. All results also hold for quantum spin systems.

papers.abstract: Environmental fluctuations constitute a major source of decoherence in quantum devices, rendering their spectral characterization essential for robust control and error correction. Existing qubit noise spectroscopy methods often rely on elaborate control sequences or extensive scans over evolution t…

papers.abstract: Spin squeezing is a genuine multipartite entanglement resource enabling quantum-enhanced metrology beyond classical limits. Based on a hybrid solid-state system of nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers and magnons, we propose a scheme for generating spin squeezing via Kerr nonlinearity. In the large-detunin…

papers.abstract: The strongly correlated phases of the homogeneous electron gas constitute the vocabulary of many-body condensed matter physics and find a natural realization in semiconductors. In this setting, recent neural-network variational Monte Carlo calculations discovered an unexpected quantum phase of matte…

papers.title: SimPoly: Simulation of polymers with machine learning force fields derived from first principles
papers.abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 09 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78736-xThe authors develop a machine learning force field trained only on quantum-chemical data that can reproduce measured key polymer properties such as densities and glass transition temperatures.

papers.title: Calpain-mediated TBP cleavage disturbs neuronal AMOT-YAP1 signalling
papers.abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 09 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79055-xTBP fragments activate calpains and disrupt AMOT-YAP1 signalling, revealing a pathway involved in normal neural development and implicated in spinocerebellar ataxia type 17.

papers.title: Topological Josephson trijunctions as a Majorana source and path
papers.abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 07 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79077-5Manipulating Majorana bound states is a key requirement for topological quantum computation. Here, the authors propose a topological insulator Josephson trijunction in a magnetic field that enables the generation, transport, and fusion of Majorana bound states through static control of superconducting phases.

papers.title: Global Two-Sided Estimates for Time-Fractional Diffusion Kernels on Hyperbolic Space
papers.abstract: We study time-fractional diffusion on real hyperbolic space $\mathbb H^n$, $n\ge2$, with Caputo order $0<α<1$. We establish global two-sided pointwise estimates for the homogeneous fundamental kernel $Z_{\mathbb H}(t,r)$ and the inhomogeneous (Duhamel) kernel $Y_{\mathbb H}(t,r)$, uniformly over all $t>0$ and positive geodesic distances $r$. By combining inverse-stable subordination with global bounds for the hyperbolic heat kernel, we distinguish a short-time local regime, a large-time interior region, and an exterior region governed by a saddle-point problem with parameter $r/t$. Both kernels have the same exterior exponential rate, while their amplitudes are related by an explicit saddle-point factor. The estimates are uniformly comparable on the interfaces between regimes, recover the Euclidean time-fractional singularities at small scales, and identify the influence of hyperbolic geometry on large-scale decay. The kernel $Z_{\mathbb H}$ also describes the one-time marginal density of hyperbolic Brownian motion under an independent inverse stable clock. This representation yields a radial limit law, moment and quantile asymptotics, and a change in the mean square displacement from order $t^α$ at small times to order $t^{2α}$ at large times.

papers.title: Directed systems of A-spaces and weak cores
papers.abstract: We prove that for any regular CW-complex $X$ there exists a quotient map $X\to Y$ that is a weak homotopy equivalence and which is minimal with that property, meaning that any quotient $Y\to Z$ that is a weak equivalence, must be a homeomorphism. The space $Y$ we obtain is an Alexandroff space: a space in which arbitrary intersections of open sets are open. The weak core $Y$ of $X$ is not unique in general. We study homotopy invariants preserved by filtered colimits of Alexandroff spaces. This can be seen as an analogous to Stong's theory of cores of finite topological spaces.

papers.title: On the (non-)closedness of the set of ReLU networks
papers.abstract: We prove that the set $\mathcal{N}_N$ of ReLU networks with one hidden layer and at most $N\in\mathbb N$ neurons is weakly closed in $W^{1,p}(Ω)$, for a bounded connected open set $Ω\subset\mathbb R^d$. Consequently, every coercive, weakly lower semicontinuous energy on this space attains its minimum over $\mathcal{N}_N$. This covers the Deep Ritz method with convex integrands, Sobolev training and Lipschitz learning. Moreover, as the weight decay parameter tends to zero, minimizers of the regularized problem converge, up to subsequences, to minimizers with minimal parameter norm. We also prove that the set of ReLU networks with two hidden layers of bounded widths is not closed in $W^{1,p}(Ω)$ or in $C(\overlineΩ)$. This disproves a conjecture of Petersen, Raslan and Voigtlaender.

papers.title: Unconditional Uniqueness of KdV and mKdV Green Solutions at Low Regularity
papers.abstract: We prove unconditional uniqueness for the Korteweg--de Vries (KdV) equation in $C_tH^{-1}_x(\mathbb R)$ and the real defocusing modified KdV equation in $C_tL^2_x(\mathbb R)$ within the class of Green solutions, an intrinsically well defined solution notion that encodes the evolution at these low regularities through the diagonal Green functions of the associated Lax operators. A key contribution is automatic local smoothing: the Green identities imply $q\in L^2_{\mathrm{loc}}$ for KdV and $u_x,u^2\in L^2_{\mathrm{loc}}$ for mKdV in spacetime, with estimates uniform over spatial translates. The uniqueness results therefore identify every Green solution in these classes with the continuous extension of the corresponding Schwartz flow.

papers.title: Analytic information encoded in the Bernstein-Sato polynomial of genus-one plane branches
papers.abstract: We give an explicit formula recovering the Zariski invariant of a plane branch with one Puiseux pair from its Bernstein-Sato polynomial. Thus the Bernstein-Sato stratification refines the Zariski-invariant stratification. We determine the generic roots in each stratum from the value semigroup and the Zariski invariant, refining Yano's description for a fixed topological class. We also compute the maximal spectral-exponent discrepancy and relate it to the dimension of the generic Bernstein-Sato locus and the minimum Tjurina number.

papers.title: Novikov-Magnus Master Equation for Driven Quantum Systems under Classical Correlated Noise
papers.abstract: We introduce a modular framework for deriving time-local quantum master equations for driven systems subject to temporally correlated classical noise. The construction combines the Donsker-Furutsu-Novikov relation with the Magnus expansion: Functional response closes the noise average, while nested commutators retain the noncommuting chronological action of noise-induced perturbations along the controlled quantum trajectory. For zero-mean Gaussian noise, we derive the resulting Novikov-Magnus quantum master equation through fourth order in the noise strength. The same response hierarchy suggests a natural extension beyond Gaussian noise, with connected higher-order noise correlations weighting higher functional derivatives of the stochastic map. For a driven qubit under Ornstein-Uhlenbeck and band-limited $1/f$ noise, the second- and fourth-order maps remain CPTP throughout the perturbative regime and accurately reproduce stochastic simulations. Their diamond-norm errors are comparable to those of the cumulant-based pseudo-Lindblad master equation, with a modest fourth-order improvement for Ornstein-Uhlenbeck noise.

papers.title: Pure mapping class group fixed points in $\mathrm{PU}(2,1)$
papers.abstract: We classify all the fixed points for the action of the pure mapping class group on $\mathrm{PU}(2,1)$ character varieties of surface groups. Up to trivial peripheral monodromies, we prove that the irreducible fixed points are either pair of pants representations, or restrictions of reduced Burau representations to a once-punctured torus and restrictions of reduced Gassner representations to a 4-punctured sphere. On the other hand, we prove that the only non-trivial reducible fixed points appear in genus 0 where they map all but at most three peripheral loops in the centralizer of the image, and in genus 1 where they are valued in the quaternion group $H_8$. As consequences, we deduce (i) that an irreducible representation in genus 0 with at least four non-trivial peripheral monodromies is rigid if and only if it is a fixed point, and (ii) a partial classification of irreducible representations of pure braid groups into $\mathrm{PU}(2,1)$.

papers.title: Trajectory-Dependent Decoherence and Leakage During Shuttling of Multi-Spin Qubits
papers.abstract: Logical qubits encoded in collective states of multiple spins are promising building blocks for large-scale semiconductor quantum processors. As novel fault-tolerant architectures increasingly rely on qubit shuttling, understanding decoherence of the shuttled multi-spin qubits becomes crucial. We analyze fidelity and leakage of the logical qubits dephased by the spatio-temporally correlated $1/f$ noise, considering two-, three-, and four-spin encodings. We study different shuttling protocols and establish that for all encodings generally, parallel shuttling provides the best protection against decoherence at short distances, whereas sequential shuttling outperforms others for long-range transport (although the exact boundaries depend on the specific device parameters). We explain this common behavior in terms of the dephasing factors of pairs of the shuttled spins; we provide explicit expressions for fidelities and leakage, thus enabling experimentalists to predict performance of the multi-spin qubits from only several independently measured pairwise dephasing factors. Our results establish a connection between shuttling trajectories, noise correlations, and qubit decoherence, and provide guidance for achieving noise-resilient shuttling in scalable semiconductor quantum processors.

papers.title: Finitely Presented Covers of Topological Full Groups
papers.abstract: Commutator subgroups of infinite minimal subshifts provide the first examples of infinite, finitely generated, simple amenable groups. We prove that if $G$ is a finitely presented group which maps onto the commutator subgroup of the topological full group of an infinite minimal subshift, then $G$ contains a non-abelian free subgroup. This in particular implies that these groups are not finitely presented. We also show that the topological full group of an irreducible subshift of finite type contains non-abelian free subgroups.

papers.title: A Quantum Mechanical Description of Active Matter
papers.abstract: The natural environments habitable to life are inseparable from dissipative and entropic forces, which mandate active matter to operate on constant fluxes of energy and momentum to survive and propagate through spacetime. In contrast to fundamental particles which are characterized by energy and momentum, we postulate that energy expenditure rate and momentum generation rate are the fundamental dynamical quantities driving this evolution of swimming active matter and accordingly construct the corresponding Lagrangian and Hamiltonian of motion of the active matter. Furthermore, living systems broadly employ periodic, non-repeating motion for both locomotion and various biological functions, with meaningful information stored in the periods of these functions. Consequently, analyzing these dynamics in the Fourier space lands us at the familiar tools of the operator based, quantum mechanics. This is accomplished by introducing a complex field to describe the evolving probability distribution of a single unit, as well as the population density of mutually non-interacting active particles under the constraint of scarce resources. The resulting single-unit wavefunction evolves analogously to the Dirac equation with minimal coupling, wherein gauge symmetry reflects the generality of the governing equations across arbitrary resource landscapes. Additionally, we present a Schrödinger-like equation where the effective potential term represents the environmentally mandated, non-motile base metabolic rate. Finally, we formalize the bidirectional coupling between active swimmers and the surrounding fluid via a multipole expansion of the active force with an emphasis on force monopoles and dipoles, where each pole corresponds to a distinct mode of active motility.

papers.title: Geometric Pairwise Classification of Affine Constraints over Ellipsoidal Regions
papers.abstract: This paper presents a deterministic geometric procedure for analysing affine constraints over fixed ellipsoidal regions, motivated by chance-constrained set approximation. Analytical tests classify inequalities as always violated, never violated, or cutting. Pairwise tests determine whether two inequalities can be strictly violated at a common point, yielding a compatibility matrix. The tests follow from quadratic optimisation and the Karush--Kuhn--Tucker conditions, with explicit treatment of tangencies, parallel normals, and degenerate inequalities. The formulation applies in arbitrary finite dimensions and provides geometric information for subsequent bounds on simultaneous sampled violations and safe-region approximation.

papers.title: Large-Time Behavior and Asymptotic Profiles for Time-Fractional Nonlinear Diffusion Equations via Entropy Methods
papers.abstract: We investigate the large-time behavior of nonnegative solutions to the time-fractional nonlinear diffusion equation $\partial_t^α(u-u_0) = Δu^m$, $0<α<1$, $m>0$, in a bounded domain with the homogeneous Dirichlet boundary condition. We prove that the rescaled solution $t^{\fracα{m}}u$ converges as $t\to\infty$ to an asymptotic profile $S$ characterized by $-ΔS^m = u_0/Γ(1-α)$. Moreover, we show that $t^αu^m$ converges to $S^m$, which admits an explicit representation in terms of the Green function and the initial datum. In contrast to the classical case $α=1$, the asymptotic profile depends explicitly on the initial datum.

papers.title: Raman anyon-Hubbard model in a 1D Bose lattice gas
papers.abstract: The anyon-Hubbard model is the paradigmatic lattice model of one-dimensional (1D) anyons, in which chiral interactions make bosons equivalent to particles with fractional statistics. Its continuum limit, the chiral BF theory, emerges as the low-energy description of a Raman-coupled Bose gas with imbalanced interactions. Here, we show that loading such a gas into a 1D optical lattice realizes the lattice counterpart of this theory, which we name the Raman anyon-Hubbard model. The Raman-dressed bosons acquire density-dependent Peierls phases when tunneling through occupied sites. For a small statistical phase, the model reduces to the anyon-Hubbard model, while beyond this limit it defines a distinct lattice anyon model with unbounded rather than periodic statistical interactions. Numerically, we show that the dressed gas displays the defining properties of 1D anyons, namely a density-dependent asymmetry of the ground-state momentum distribution, interaction-induced asymmetric transport and chiral bound states. Remarkably, these features are readily accessible with Raman-coupled $^{39}$K atoms, opening up the experimental exploration of 1D anyons beyond the few-particle regime.

papers.title: Efficient iterative methods for the nonlinear compressible Reynolds equation with Navier slip boundary condition
papers.abstract: In this study, we present a comparison of iterative methods for the compressible Reynolds equation with Navier slip boundary conditions, based on a fully compressible cavitation model for lubricated bearings. We establish the existence and uniqueness of the solution to the two-dimensional problem. We introduce the Kirchhoff transformation to reformulate the nonlinear density-pressure relationship into a quasi-linear problem. We develop an efficient numerical approach to solve the two-dimensional nonlinear problem. The methods examined are the Gauss-Seidel method, the Newton-Raphson method and parallelized nonlinear Jacobi method, applied to one- and two-dimensional slider bearing configurations. The overall solution time is shown to depend strongly on the choice of method.

papers.title: Classical control of quantum-state relaxation in confined molecular hydrogen
papers.abstract: Quantum-state conversion between the ortho and para nuclear-spin states of H$_2$ is forbidden in the isolated molecule but these states can become connected through interactions with a surrounding environment. How that same environment governs the dynamics of the newly connected states remains poorly understood. Here, we investigate this problem using H$_2$ confined in crystalline molecular solids, where the host environment selectively enables conversion between a pair of otherwise disconnected ortho-H$_2$ and para-H$_2$ states. Rotationally resolved infrared spectroscopy directly determines the state-specific conversion dynamics in crystalline CO$_2$ and N$_2$O at 10 K, revealing that increasing H$_2$ concentration suppresses nuclear-spin conversion by nearly an order of magnitude, reaching complete suppression by 20% H$_2$ loading. Molecular dynamics and Monte Carlo simulations identify two complementary origins of this concentration dependence: changes in the thermally populated phonon modes available to mediate relaxation, and strain-driven H$_2$ clustering that progressively removes molecules from the host crystal field responsible for enabling conversion. The resulting picture connects a classical collective response of the host to microscopic quantum-state dynamics: H$_2$ loading generates strain that reorganizes the local molecular environment, thereby modifying both the phonon bath and the molecular coupling to that bath. These results establish a multiscale mechanism by which condensed-phase environments can govern the connectivity and dynamics of an effective two-level system.

papers.title: Deformations and Local Geometry of Lie Triple System Morphisms
papers.abstract: In this paper, first we study the deformations, stability and rigidity of Lie triple system morphisms by means of higher derived brackets and augmented Yamaguti cohomology. The vanishing of the first cohomology gives formal and local inner rigidity. The vanishing of the second cohomology removes the formal extension obstructions and, in finite dimension over $\mathbb{R}$, gives local smoothness and stability under simultaneous perturbations of the two products. Next, we establish the relationship with Lie algebra homomorphisms in each part of the theory. The universal enveloping Lie algebra identifies a Lie triple morphism with a grading-preserving Lie homomorphism. We obtain the corresponding first cohomology isomorphism, the equivalence of formal and smooth deformations, and a stability result for graded Lie bracket perturbations. For Lie triple products induced by binary Lie brackets, we construct a comparison of differentials and obstruction classes. Under perfectness and a zero-centralizer condition, the local morphism spaces coincide. Finally, we relate triple subsystem graphs to graded Lie subalgebra graphs and compare their normal differentials.

papers.title: Local fluctuations, majorization, and nontransitivity in cube tilings of $\mathbb{Z}^d$
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{P}$ be a partition of $\mathbb{Z}^d$ into translates of the discrete unit cube $\{0,1\}^d$. For a uniformly chosen $\varepsilon\in\{0,1\}^d$, we count the cubes of $\mathcal{P}$ entirely contained in the observation window $[0,3]^d+\varepsilon$.
