When $(H,R)$ is factorizable, we show that $(R_H(A),K_{\mathrm{ref}}(A))$ is isomorphic, as a quasitriangular left $H$-comodule algebra, to $A\otimes H$ equipped with the trivial left $H$-coaction on $A$ and the universal $K$-matrix induced by $R_{21}R$. In this case, we also classify all universal $K$-matrices on $R_H(A)$. Finally, we prove that $(R_H(A),K_{\mathrm{ref}}(A))$ is factorizable if and only if $(H,R)$ is factorizable and $A$ is simple as an algebra.

papers.title: Computing Invariant Reachable Sets through Sum-of-Squares Programming
papers.abstract: Funnels, time-varying invariant sets around nominal trajectories, certify that a closed-loop system tracks its plan, and can be composed into verified motion plans. Their computation by sum-of-squares (SOS) programming is well established in formulation but not in practice: the result depends on implementation choices such as the initial guess, Lyapunov function normalization, and termination rule, which the literature documents only briefly. This paper presents a self-contained treatment of SOS-based funnel computation, implemented in the open-source package computeSOSFunnels. We propose a minimum-volume formulation with inlet and outlet constraints under which funnels with coinciding nominal endpoints compose by construction. Numerical experiments on a unicycle, with timing studies on a cart-pole and a 12-state quadrotor, characterize the pipeline: infeasible initial guesses are partly decidable before solving, the certificate shows no violations among 39,000 boundary samples per funnel under the true dynamics, and constructing the semidefinite program, not solving it, dominates computation time.

papers.title: Canonical Projectivization of Algebraic Varieties in Characteristic Zero
papers.abstract: We construct a canonical projectivization of every smooth proper algebraic variety $X$ in characteristic zero. Once a principalization procedure is fixed, the construction gives a finite sequence of blowups in smooth centers with smooth projective endpoint, natural under semilinear isomorphisms and preserving the quasi-projective core, the intersection of all maximal quasi-projective open subsets. At each stage we select finitely many ideals near the generic points of the image in $X$ of the boundary of a maximal quasi-projective open. Principalizing their product strictly lowers the dimension of that image. The selection is defined intrinsically, without a polarization or a chosen projective modification; a Hilbert scheme argument proves its finiteness. Naturality embeds the automorphism group in that of a smooth projective variety of the same dimension. We then extend the construction to smooth proper integral algebraic spaces, obtaining canonical projectivizations of all compact connected Moishezon manifolds.

papers.title: Beyond Expected Profit: How Risk Aversion Alters Learning in the Data-Driven Newsvendor
papers.abstract: We study how risk aversion changes learning and the value of data in the classical newsvendor problem. We evaluate data-driven policies through the Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR) of realized loss on the combined draw of an i.i.d.\ historical sample and an independent future demand from the same distribution. We measure worst-case regret over demand distributions on a bounded interval relative to an oracle that knows the distribution. We show that, for every fixed positive risk level, Sample Average Approximation (SAA) can retain regret bounded away from zero as the sample size \(n\) grows, even at a fixed demand distribution, and characterize its asymptotic worst-case regret. We trace this failure to persistent variability in the learned order, which contributes to tail risk under this combined-risk evaluation. We establish that risk aversion also slows the minimax learning rate over all data-driven policies from \(Θ(n^{-1/2})\) under expectation to \(Θ(n^{-1/4})\). We construct policies that average nearby order statistics and attain this optimal rate. For finite samples, we reduce worst-case analysis for mixtures of convex combinations of order statistics to Bernoulli demand on the endpoints of the interval. We use this reduction to formulate a linear program for computing minimax policies within this class to any accuracy. In numerical experiments, we find that minimizing this objective alone can leave substantial average CVaR regret when each learned order is evaluated over future demand alone. We therefore develop a two-stage linear program that minimizes the worst-case value of this average regret while allowing a prescribed increase in the original objective. This yields improvements across a broad range of scenarios. Our results show that risk aversion changes both the rate at which data improve decisions and the policies needed to realize that improvement.

papers.title: Almost sure exponential stability of multi-dimensional stochastic systems driven by a symmetric $α$-stable process
papers.abstract: This article investigates the stability of a class of multidimensional stochastic systems driven by a symmetric $α$-stable process with $1<α<2$. These driving processes have infinite second moments, which prevents the direct application of standard second-moment methods and may lead to divergent jump integrals in the generators of quadratic Lyapunov functions. We establish criteria for $p$th-moment exponential stability and almost sure exponential stability. A numerical example illustrates the theoretical results.

papers.title: Approximate Synthetic Spectra of Quantum Systems Associated with Compact Lie Groups
papers.abstract: How can noncommuting quantum observables retain the geometry of a classical phase space? Motivated by Mumford's question on approximately macroscopically unique (AMU) states and the work of Lin and Wang, we study synthetic spectra of position--momentum and angular-momentum systems. Under the hypotheses of their AMU theorems, nonempty synthetic spectra yield AMU states. For sufficiently small $\hbar$, the position--momentum spectrum fills the plane, while the angular-momentum spectrum contains any prescribed ball. The latter calculation leads to compact Lie groups: we prove that highest-weight coadjoint orbits lie in regional synthetic spectra under an explicit variance bound. Function-space representations of $SU(n)$, $SO(n)$, and $Sp(n)$ provide further examples.

papers.title: Fractional colorings of $K_r$-free graphs with local demands
papers.abstract: We study fractional coloring with local demands, a framework introduced by Kelly and Postle in which one seeks a probability distribution on the independent sets of a graph such that each vertex $v$ is included with probability at least a prescribed target $φ(v)$. For $K_r$-free graphs, Kelly and Postle conjectured that such a distribution exists provided $φ(v)\le c_r\frac{\log d(v)}{d(v)}$ for a fixed \(c_r>0\), where $d(v)$ is the degree of $v$, and they established this up to a factor of $(\log\log d(v))^2$. In this paper, we prove their conjecture, showing that \[ φ(v)\le\frac{c}{r}\frac{\log(d(v)+2)}{d(v)+1} \] suffices for an absolute constant $c>0$. As a corollary, we obtain a lower bound on the independence number of $K_r$-free graphs in terms of their degree sequence. This strengthens the bound that OpenAI proved in resolving the Ajtai-Erdős-Komlós-Szemerédi conjecture. Moreover, our argument yields a deterministic algorithm that produces the desired probability distribution in time $2^{O(r^2)}n^{O(1)}$, where \(n\) is the number of vertices and the implied constants are absolute.

papers.title: State Evolution and Universality of Iterated Linear Programs for the Binary Perceptron
papers.abstract: The binary perceptron is a random constraint satisfaction problem that asks for a sign vector satisfying a system of random linear inequalities. Its solution space has a strikingly extreme geometry: at every positive constraint density, all but a vanishing fraction of the solutions are isolated. Yet polynomial-time algorithms find solutions at small enough constraint density, which raises the question of how efficient algorithms navigate such a landscape. Linear programming is a natural algorithm to study here, but its analysis has so far been limited to a single round. Li, Schramm, and Zhou (STOC 2025) analyzed one linear program followed by iterative rounding. In this work, we overcome this limitation and give a precise analysis of iterated linear programming for the binary perceptron. (1) For Gaussian matrices and any fixed number of rounds, we characterize the iterated linear programs exactly through a deterministic state-evolution recursion. (2) Adding a final rounding step, we obtain a randomized polynomial-time algorithm for the binary perceptron. Numerical evaluations of the recursion provide evidence that it succeeds at constraint density $α=0.60$ with zero margin, well beyond the range $α\le0.1$ guaranteed by the single-LP analysis and $α\approx0.327$ (Jo and Lee, 2026), the best guarantee so far. (3) We establish universality, showing that the same characterization holds for matrices with i.i.d. entries drawn from any centered, unit-variance subgaussian law. The key idea of our proof is that, although conditioning on earlier rounds makes the matrix non-Gaussian, its conditional law can be computed explicitly and remains close to a Gaussian law, so the convex Gaussian min-max theorem applies in every round. For universality, we compare Gaussian and subgaussian matrices through the Lindeberg principle, using a regularized version of each linear program.

papers.title: Conjecture B for $X_{10}$ and its genus-two mirror
papers.abstract: We prove Conjecture B of Akhtar--Coates--Corti--Heuberger--Kasprzyk--Oneto--Petracci--Prince--Tveiten unconditionally for the normalized family of maximally mutable Laurent polynomials with prescribed $T$-binomial edge coefficients associated with the degree-10 orbifold del Pezzo hypersurface $X_{10}\subset\mathbb{P}(1,2,3,5)$. An explicit $S$-extended quantum-period calculation determines the affine mirror map $λ=a-346$ and proves that the regularized quantum period equals the classical period as a formal power series throughout the family.

papers.title: How Risky Is Your Data-Driven Policy?
papers.abstract: Data-driven algorithms are ubiquitous across industries, and there is an extensive literature on analyzing their \emph{average} performance. The risk profile of such algorithms, while critical, is much less understood. This paper quantifies the risk of data-driven policies and isolates its sources. We evaluate a policy through the conditional value-at-risk (CVaR) of its loss over the training sample, any policy randomization, and the future outcome, at a fixed unknown distribution. Regret against an oracle that knows the distribution decomposes into expected post-sample regret (PS), the average outcome-only CVaR gap of the selected action, and a sample-risk premium (SR), the additional tail risk omitted by averaging those evaluations. The analogous premium vanishes under expected loss. We characterize when the premium vanishes and how large it is relative to post-sample regret. For losses with a continuous density near the tail cutoff, we identify conditions under which both components decay at the same rate, yet the limiting ratio of the premium to post-sample regret can reach the thousands. When a probability mass at the cutoff moves with the action, the premium can decay more slowly and dominate post-sample regret. We establish conditions under which sample average approximation learns the oracle action at rate $n^{-1/2}$ in both settings, but its combined-risk regret is of order $n^{-1}$ in the first and $n^{-1/2}$ in the second. In finite-sample numerical examples of SAA in both settings, the premium accounts for approximately $74\%$--$97\%$ of regret.

papers.title: An example of universal braiding in Links--Gould topological quantum computation
papers.abstract: We construct a universal quantum computational encoding via braiding in Links--Gould fusion spaces associated to $U_q^H(\mathfrak{sl}(2|1))$ where $q$ is on the unit circle and is not a root of unity. The construction uses only neglectons and is realized in the morphism spaces $\mathrm{Hom}_{U_q^H}(V(0,α),V(0,-\frac{1}{2})^{\otimes 2N}\otimes V(0,α)).$ Under explicit positivity and arithmetic constraints these spaces admit a $2^N$-dimensional computational subspace with a positive definite Hermitian form. We prove single-qubit density in $\mathrm{U}(2,1)$ and approximate arbitrary unitary operators on $N$-qubit computational subspaces with arbitrarily small leakage. The calculations use explicit inclusions, projections, and Hermitian pairings without requiring $F$-matrices.

papers.title: Inferential Issues in Model-based Small Area Estimation: Some History and Selective Recent Advances
papers.abstract: Model-based Small Area Estimation (SAE) has seen rapid growth over the past 25 years or so due to the rapidly increasing demand for reliable small area estimators of totals, means and more complex area parameters. Direct area-specific estimators are either unreliable (due to small area-specific sample sizes) or not feasible (due to zero area-specific sample sizes). It is therefore necessary to borrow strength from related areas through implicit or explicit models linking related areas. We focus on explicit area-level and unit-level models. After a brief historical sketch of the evolution of SAE, we focus on selective recent developments (mostly after 2015). Developments before 2015 are mostly covered in the comprehensive Wiley book by Rao and Molina (2015). Under a basic area-level model, we consider semi-parametric and robust estimation of small area means under model misspecifications. Under a basic unit level model, methods for estimating complex parameters, such as poverty indicators, will be presented, including robust estimation in the presence of outliers. A comparison of area-level and unit-level models when unit level data are available will also be presented. Estimation methods studied include empirical best linear unbiased prediction (EBLUP), empirical best (EB) and hierarchical Bayes (HB).

papers.title: Testing Implies Distance Estimation with Polynomial Loss
papers.abstract: A tester decides whether a graph has a property or is far from having it. A distance estimator asks for more: it must approximately determine how many edges need to be changed. A property is said to be testable if there is a tester with a number of queries bounded independently of the graph's order for each conceivable distance. Similarly, if a property admits an estimator with a number of queries bounded independently of the graph's order, it is said to be estimable. Fischer and Newman proved that, in the dense graph model, every testable property is also estimable. We show that the passage from testing to estimation requires only a polynomial increase in query complexity. This resolves a long-standing open problem in property testing, previously tackled by Fiat and Ron, by Hoppen, Kohayakawa, Lang, Lefmann, and Stagni, and by Gishboliner, Kushnir, and Shapira.

papers.title: The $p$-local topologoical period-index problem in dimensions $2p+2$ and below
papers.abstract: For any odd prime number $p$, we solve the topological period-index problem for a $p$-primary element of the Brauer group of a CW-complex of dimension not greater than $2p+2$.

papers.title: Information-Geometric Representation of Upper Bounds on Fluctuation Growth in Open Quantum Systems
papers.abstract: Building on our earlier results for closed quantum systems, we investigate the dynamical evolution of quantum fluctuations and their connections to Fisher information and the quantum operations describing open-system dynamics. Starting from a general expression for the time derivative of an observable's uncertainty, we derive an alternative upper bound on fluctuation growth in an open quantum system using the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality. The resulting bound separates contributions from the evolution of the quantum state and the explicit time dependence of the observable, reducing to a known result for closed-system dynamics. We then establish a connection between fluctuation dynamics and quantum Fisher information by decomposing the density operator and the symmetric logarithmic derivative (SLD) into coherent and incoherent contributions, which leads to a bound relating the evolution of observable uncertainty to the coherent and incoherent components of the Fisher information, providing an information-geometric interpretation of fluctuation growth. To connect fluctuation dynamics with quantum operations governing open-system evolutions, we derive the time evolution of the eigenvalues of the density operator in terms of Kraus operators. Using the infinitesimal-time relation between Kraus and Lindblad operators, we obtain a corresponding expression for the eigenvalue dynamics in terms of Lindblad operators. This formulation directly relates changes in the density operator eigenvalues to the quantum processes acting on the system. We then study the results using some examples. Our results provide a framework connecting observable fluctuation growth, Fisher information, and the Kraus and Lindblad descriptions of quantum evolution, offering a route toward understanding how specific quantum channels influence the information and fluctuations available in an evolving quantum system.

papers.title: A note on the BRST-BV Formalism Explanation of Deformation Quantization and Algebraic Index Theorem
papers.abstract: In this note, we begin with considering the simple one-dimensional field theory describing a single free particle on manifold, and apply the BRST formalism and BV quantization to this model following the standard procedures in physics. Through calculations that, while not fully rigorous, have a more transparent physical interpretation, then subsequent geometric identifications, we recover the deformation quantization and algebraic index theorem on symplectic manifold. This note thus elucidates the physical origins and mechanisms of these mathematical results.

papers.title: Non-centered maximal operators over $\ell^q$ balls for exponential and Laguerre-type measures
papers.abstract: We establish the \(L^p\)-boundedness, \(1<p<\infty\), of the non-centered Hardy--Littlewood maximal operator associated with \(\ell^q\) balls, \(1<q<\infty\), for the non-radial exponential measure \[ dμ(x)=e^{-|x_1|-\cdots-|x_d|}\,dx \] in every dimension \(d\ge1\). This settles the higher-dimensional Euclidean case left open by Nowak, Sasso, Sjögren and Stempak, and extends their results to the full range \(1<q<\infty\). We also prove that these operators are not of weak type \((1,1)\) when \(d\ge2\). Together with the known results for \(q=1\) and \(q=\infty\) for the exponential measure, this gives a complete description of the \(L^p\)-boundedness and weak type \((1,1)\) behavior for all \(1\le q\le\infty\). {We also extend the strong \(L^p\)-boundedness to the Laguerre-type measures \(dμ_α(x)=\prod_{j=1}^d|x_j|^{α_j}e^{-|x_1|-\cdots-|x_d|}\,dx\) for all \(α_j\ge0\) and \(1\le q\le\infty\), and for the full range \(α_j>-1\) when \(q=\infty\).} {The main arguments rely} on geometric estimates for sections of \(\ell^q\) balls and a slicing argument.

papers.title: Weighted Fractional Commutator Estimate and Application to the Fractional Wave Equations with Time-dependent Damping
papers.abstract: In this paper, we first establish a weighted bilinear fractional commutator estimate involving the spatial weight $\langle x \rangle^{2m}$. This estimate provides a powerful tool to resolve the difficulties arising from the nonlocality of the fractional Laplacian $(-Δ)^{σ/2}$ and the interaction between the unbounded weights and the nonlocal operator at infinity. We then apply this result to investigate the Cauchy problem for the fractional wave equation with time-dependent damping and source nonlinearity: $$ \begin{cases} \partial_t^2 u(t,x) + (-Δ)^{σ/2} u(t,x) + b(t) \partial_t u(t,x) = |u(t,x)|^p, & (t,x) \in (0,T) \times \mathbb{R}^N, \\ u(0,x) = \varepsilon u_0(x), \quad \partial_t u(0,x) = \varepsilon u_1(x), & x \in \mathbb{R}^N, \end{cases} $$ where $σ\in (0,2)$, the initial data scale with a small parameter $\varepsilon > 0$, and the time-dependent damping coefficient $b(t)$ satisfies $b(t) \approx (1+t)^{-β}$ for $β\in [-1, 1)$. Utilizing scaling variables and constructing a weighted energy framework based on Theorem 1.1, we derive a priori differential inequalities for the total energy. For the supercritical case $p > p_c := 1 + \fracσ{N}$, we prove the small-data global existence and uniqueness of strong solutions in weighted Sobolev spaces $H^{σ/2,m}(\mathbb{R}^N) \times H^{0,m}(\mathbb{R}^N)$ by closing a bootstrap argument. For the subcritical ($1 < p < p_c$) and critical ($p = p_c$) cases, we establish precise lower bounds for the lifespan $T_\varepsilon$ of blow-up solutions via delicate ODE analysis. Together with the corresponding upper estimates, our results fully determine the sharp lifespan estimates for all $β\in [-1, 1)$, confirming that $p_c = 1 + \fracσ{N}$ is indeed the critical exponent for the fractional wave equation with time-dependent damping.

papers.title: Limit cycles of singular algebraic foliations on the real projective plane
papers.abstract: In this paper we consider cycles of singular algebraic foliations on the real projective plane. Our first result shows that there exists a limit cycle of singular algebraic foliations such that the limit cycle cannot be realized in any affine chart, that is, it fails to appear in any affine plane via the usual dehomogenization. On the other hand, under an appropriate convexity assumption, we verify that a cycle becomes fully visible, lying entirely in some affine chart. We then analyze the accumulation behavior of limit cycles of singular algebraic foliations on the real projective plane. Last we prove that algebraic foliations of degree at most two on the real projective plane have only finitely many limit cycles, and the maximum number of limit cycle is zero, one and at least six for algebraic foliations of degree zero, one and two on the real projective plane, respectively. This result extends Bamon's finiteness theorem for quadratic affine vector fields in [Publ. Math. IHÉS, (64)1986, pp. 111--142].

papers.title: Smooth and Topological Nonorientable Four-Genera of Low-Crossing Knots
papers.abstract: We compare linking-form bounds with the smooth and locally flat nonorientable 4-genera of low-crossing knots. For every prime knot with at most 13 crossings whose Witt-level linking-form bound is at least 2, this bound equals both genera. We also exhibit 41 prime knots with 12 or 13 crossings that bound locally flat Möbius bands but no smooth ones, and whose smooth nonorientable 4-genus is 2. Our methods combine linking forms, Heegaard Floer correction terms and definite-lattice obstructions with explicit band constructions. They determine 3,300 of the 3,525 values left unknown in KnotInfo on 2 November 2026; the remaining 225 knots have range $[1,2]$. We obtain new lower bounds of 2 for 2,102 knots with 14 crossings and correct previously reported values for three knots with 11 crossings.

papers.title: Galois-modular obstructions to the categorification of near-group fusion rings
papers.abstract: In this article we establish new obstructions to the categorification of near-group fusion rings by combining the values of irreducible characters of the Grothendieck ring with the Galois symmetry of the induced unit object $I(1)$ in the Drinfeld center. As a result, we show that a near-group ring of type $G+m$, where $G$ is an abelian group and both $|G|$ and $m$ are odd, can only categorify if $m=|G|$.

papers.title: Thermally enhanced magnon-phonon resonance in van der Waals antiferromagnet FePS3
papers.abstract: Strong coupling between collective excitations provides a route to controlling quantum states of matter, yet its evolution under thermal fluctuations remains poorly understood. In the van der Waals antiferromagnet FePS3, strong magnon-phonon coupling is established at low temperatures. At the same time, recent terahertz experiments revealed the counterintuitive stabilization of a long-lived metastable magnetic state with an exceedingly long lifetime of 5 msec at the antiferromagnetic transition, not at the base temperature. This was attributed to a strongly coupled spin-lattice scenario, challenging the conventional wisdom that increased magnetic and thermal fluctuations near TN should be detrimental to the coherent control of a metastable phase. Thus it requires an independent examination for correct understanding. Using high-field Raman spectroscopy, we systematically investigate the temperature evolution of magnon-phonon coupling in FePS3. We observe a pronounced avoided crossing between magnon and phonon modes across a wide range of temperatures and find that the coupling strength remains remarkably robust with increasing temperatures. The zero-field magnon-phonon detuning decreases progressively with warming, driving the system toward resonance and thereby enhancing their hybridization near the transition temperature. This anomalous thermal evolution provides the crucial key to understanding the unusual terahertz-driven states recently reported in FePS3. More broadly, our results highlight van der Waals magnets as a promising platform for strong coupling among collective excitations and for controlling magnetic states through light-matter interactions.

papers.title: It is time for a New Deal for mathematics
papers.abstract: The AI labs' vision is based on extraction (of data, wealth, and political power). Mathematicians must oppose it, moving past personal reflections and towards reforming mathematics' social contract.

papers.title: Rational points on loxodromic K3 surfaces and complex dynamics
papers.abstract: We establish an analogue of the Hilbert irreducibility theorem for all K3 surfaces over number fields that admit an automorphism of positive entropy. Our method draws ingredients from both algebraic geometry and complex dynamics.

papers.title: Point interpolation and distributional universality in flow-based generative models
papers.abstract: Motivated by the expressive power of neural ordinary differential equations in flow-based generative modeling, we study the approximation of probability measures by pushforwards generated by parameterized families of Lipschitz vector fields. For Wasserstein distances, we establish a quantitative relationship between finite-sample point interpolation and distributional approximation, and derive universality criteria based on $L^p$-approximation of transport maps. In particular, affine-invariant families containing a non-affine vector field are universal from compactly supported absolutely continuous base measures. For total variation, we show that coordinate-wise dynamics are insufficient in dimensions $d\geq 2$ and establish sufficient conditions based on one-dimensional Sobolev approximation and shear-type mixing. We further examine the role of point interpolation, establishing when different regimes relate to one another and when approximate interpolation can be made exact.

papers.title: Optimal Subsidy Design for Productive Investment across Markets
papers.abstract: We study the optimal design of investment subsidies across heterogeneous monopolistic markets subject to a common expected discounted budget. Each producer faces a regular one-dimensional demand diffusion and chooses irreversible capacity expansion through a singular stochastic control problem. The regulator values weighted consumer surplus, producer profits, and an additional benefit from installed capacity, while accounting for the excess cost of raising public funds. We characterize producers' optimal investment responses through free boundaries and reformulate the regulator's stochastic optimization problem as a deterministic optimization over investment boundaries. An integral representation then recovers the optimal subsidy schedules that implement the resulting capacity policies. Under mild conditions on the diffusions, we establish existence of optimal schedules and uniqueness of the induced investment policies. Finally, we characterize the subsidy schedule and provide numerical illustrations.

papers.title: The Characteristic Initial Value Problem for the 3D Compressible Euler Equations
papers.abstract: We prove local existence and uniqueness, propagation of Sobolev regularity, and continuation criteria results for the characteristic initial value problem for the 3D compressible Euler equations. This is the Cauchy problem with initial data given on a pair of transversally intersecting (acoustically) null hypersurfaces. The region of existence in our main theorem is a future-neighborhood of the union of the data null hypersurfaces, where the size of the neighborhood depends on various norms of the data as well as the structure of the data null hypersurfaces. We allow for any equation of state with positive sound speed, and we do not make any symmetry, irrotationality, or isentropicity assumptions. Our analysis relies on the geometric formulation of the flow derived in [Speck19], which decomposes the equations into a "wave-part" coupled to a "transport-div-curl" part. Compared to Rendall's celebrated solution of the characteristic initial value problem for wave equations [Rendall90], substantial new ideas are needed to handle the fact that the compressible Euler equations are more complicated than pure wave equations.

papers.title: A transition calculus for 0-pseudodifferential operators with applications to gas giant geometry
papers.abstract: A gas giant Riemannian metric $g$ on a compact $n$-dimensional manifold-with-boundary $M$ blows up at the boundary $\partial M$ at the rate $1/x^α$, for $α\in (0,2)$, where $x \in C^\infty(M)$ is a boundary-defining function. Such metrics arise in the modeling of acoustic waves in gaseous planets. De Hoop-Ilmavirta-Kykkänen-Mazzeo [arXiv:2403.05475] showed that, if $α> 2/n$, the Laplace-Beltrami operator $Δ_g$ is essentially self-adjoint and has discrete spectrum. Moreover, its spectrum is stable under truncations of $M$. The proof leverages the 0-calculus of Mazzeo-Melrose. We extend this theory by introducing a 0-transition calculus for studying families of 0-operators. We demonstrate a parametrix construction for $Δ_g$ that is stable under truncations. Using this, we study the behavior of the resolvent of $Δ_g$ under truncation and extend the characterization of the spectrum obtained by de Hoop-Ilmavirta-Kykkänen-Mazzeo. In particular, we prove that (on appropriate functional-analytic domains) simple eigenvalues admit asymptotic expansions in the truncation parameter $ε$ and that the corresponding eigenfunctions admit joint asymptotic expansions in $(ε, x)$.

papers.title: Quadratic Hubbard trees, automata, and ray connections
papers.abstract: We describe an algorithm that, given a postcritically finite quadratic polynomial, outputs a finite state machine whose regular language is the set of external arguments for all points on the Hubbard tree, generalizing an example of Milnor. We do this by extracting orbit portraits from angled internal addresses, and constructing a suitable Markov partition of angle intervals. A main application is computing direct ray connections between Hubbard trees in matings of quadratic polynomials. We use this to understand ray connections in quadratic matings along veins of the Mandelbrot set, and prove that first ray connections between Hubbard trees are picked up at parabolic parameters or tips of veins.

papers.title: Convergence analysis of TriCG and TriMR for symmetric quasi-definite linear systems
papers.abstract: TriCG and TriMR are two short-recurrence iterative methods introduced by Montoison and Orban [SIAM J.\ Sci.\ Comput., 43 (2021), pp.\ A2502--A2525] for solving symmetric quasi-definite linear systems. Extensive numerical experiments have demonstrated the efficiency of these two methods, but a systematic convergence analysis is still lacking. In this paper, we derive convergence bounds for the TriCG error norm and the TriMR residual norm. Numerical experiments support the theoretical results.

papers.title: Pósa-type resilience for Hamilton Berge cycles in random hypergraphs
papers.abstract: We prove a degree-sequence resilience theorem for Hamilton Berge cycles in random uniform hypergraphs. For every fixed integer $k\ge3$ and every $γ>0$, there exists $C=C(k,γ)>0$ such that if $C\log n/n^{k-1}\le p\le1$, then asymptotically almost surely every spanning subhypergraph of $H^{(k)}(n,p)$ with increasing vertex-degree sequence $g_1\le\cdots\le g_n$ satisfying \[ g_i\ge\left(\left(\frac{i}{n}\right)^{k-1}+γ\right) \binom{n-1}{k-1}p \qquad(1\le i<n/2) \] contains a Hamilton Berge cycle. The term $(i/n)^{k-1}$ agrees with the normalized asymptotic degree bound in Salia's deterministic Pósa-type theorem. Our result gives a hypergraph analogue of the random-graph theorem of Condon et al. and strengthens the sharp Dirac-type resilience theorem of Chen and Zhang at the same logarithmic probability order. The deletion-resilience formulation has optimal probability order up to constant factors. The coefficient $1$ of $(i/n)^{k-1}$ cannot be replaced by a smaller constant. The proof controls adaptive rotations and representative-edge incidences uniformly. It also gives an endpoint-growth estimate under nonuniform deletion bounds.

papers.title: Short permutation pattern waves: The complete length-five classification
papers.abstract: For a permutation pi in Sk, a pi-wave is an increasing sequence of integers whose consecutive gaps have relative order pi. Let g(pi, n) be the maximum cardinality of a pi-wave-free subset of [n], and let P(pi, r) be the least integer N such that every r-coloring of [N] contains a monochromatic pi-wave. We determine the asymptotic orders of both functions for every permutation of length at most five. Existing upper bounds and weak-wave constructions provide sharp bounds for all but eight length-five patterns in S_5. For these eight exceptional alternating patterns, we establish g(pi, n) = Theta((log n)squared) and P(pi, r) = Theta(r(log r)squared).

papers.title: Hardware-Efficient Reinforcement-Learned Scheduling for Quantum LDPC Decoders
papers.abstract: Quantum low-density parity-check (QLDPC) codes are promising for fault-tolerant quantum computing, but their decoding algorithms present significant hardware implementation challenges. Reinforcement-learned sequential belief propagation (RL-S) improves the error-correction performance of conventional belief propagation (BP) through adaptive variable-node scheduling. However, its heap-based priority management introduces substantial hardware overhead. This paper presents hardware implementations of BP, RL-S, and bucket-based reinforcement-learned BP (BRL-S) for the [[288,12,18]] bivariate bicycle QLDPC code. The BRL-S architectures employ quantized priorities and first-in, first-out (FIFO) buckets to simplify scheduling. Three configurations with two, four, and eight priority levels are evaluated. FPGA synthesis results demonstrate that BRL-S reduces lookup-table utilization by approximately 68--72% compared with RL-S. ASIC synthesis further shows reductions of 63--67% in area and 64--69% in estimated power consumption. These results demonstrate that bucket-based scheduling substantially improves the hardware efficiency of reinforcement-learned QLDPC decoders.

papers.title: Ramanujan-type congruences for the smallest parts function
papers.abstract: In a famous paper of Andrews, he defined and studied the smallest parts function $\operatorname{spt}(n)$. He showed that it satisfies the three Ramanujan-type congruences: \[ \operatorname{spt}(5n+4)\equiv0\pmod5,\qquad \operatorname{spt}(7n+5)\equiv0\pmod7,\qquad \operatorname{spt}(13n+6)\equiv0\pmod{13}. \] In a recent preprint, the author showed that these are the only "canonical'' congruences. Here, we complete the classification of Ramanujan-type congruences for $\operatorname{spt}$, showing that if $\operatorname{spt}(\ell n+b)\equiv0\pmod\ell$ for all $n\geq0$, where $\ell\geq5$ is prime, then $(\ell,b)\in\{(5,4),(7,5),(13,6)\}.$ That is, Andrews' congruences are the only Ramanujan-type congruences for $\operatorname{spt}(n)$. These results have been verified in Lean by AxiomProver.

papers.title: Poisson area and non-tangential maximal functions on manifolds with ends and applications
papers.abstract: Let $M=\mathbb R^m\sharp(\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb S^{m-n})$, where $m>n\geq3$. The full-cone Poisson area and non-tangential maximal functions fail to be of weak type $(p,p)$ for $1<p<2$. Let $K$ be the compact part joining the two ends and put $ρ(x)=1+d(x,K)$. For fixed small $c>0$, we restrict the horizontal distance from the vertex to $cρ(x)$ and retain every positive time. The resulting maximal function is of weak type $(1,1)$ and bounded on $L^p$ for $1<p\leq\infty$. The corresponding area function uses the full spatial and time gradient. It satisfies a Fefferman--Stein distribution inequality. Its $L^p$ norm is equivalent to that of $f$ for $1<p\leq2$. This area function defines a global Hardy space. We prove its $Δ$-atomic description, its injective embedding into $L^1$, its characterization by the restricted maximal function, and its real interpolation identity with $L^2$. Direct estimates for spectral-band kernels then give a Mihlin multiplier theorem from this Hardy space to $L^1$. Interpolation and duality give $L^p$ boundedness for every $1<p<\infty$.

papers.title: Friedman--Stanley cofinality without Borel completeness
papers.abstract: Friedman and Stanley asked whether an invariant Borel class of countable structures must be Borel complete whenever every countable level of their hierarchy reduces to it. We construct a counterexample in one fixed countable language. The structural counterexample and its principal supporting results have been formalized in Lean~4 and it is available on github.

papers.title: Descending Everest, Part II: Oracle Complexity of Minimizing a Sum of Convex $(L_0,L_1)$-Smooth Functions
papers.abstract: We study the minimization of the average of $n$ convex $(L_0,L_1)$-smooth functions: the Hessian norm of each function is bounded by an affine function of its gradient norm. We assume known upper bounds $R$ on the distance from the starting point to a minimizer and $δ$ on the difference between the minimum of the average and the average of the infima of the components. We derive upper and lower bounds on the oracle complexity of reaching accuracy $\varepsilon$ in function value in expectation. Up to logarithmic factors, both bounds are of order $n(1+(L_1R)^{2/3}) +\sqrt{\frac{n(L_0+L_1^2δ)R^2}{\varepsilon}+n(L_1R)^2}$. The upper bound is attained by the proposed method YETI. The method combines ideas of accelerated proximal methods and variance reduction methods with a heuristic for choosing additional points. The number of oracle calls made by the heuristic is bounded, which preserves the upper bound on the total number of queries needed to reach the target accuracy. In the experiments, YETI is compared with first-order methods on synthetic problems and Poisson regression problems. We also examine the stopping criterion and the effect of the heuristic separately. The lower bound is obtained by an explicit construction of families of instances that are hard for any first-order method.

papers.title: Higher zeroes in pointed infinity-categories
papers.abstract: We construct an endofunctor on (small) simplicial sets which freely adjoins a zero object to a (small) infinity-category, as the co-cone construction freely adjoins a terminal object. We then prove that this endofunctor induces a left adjoint to the inclusion of the infinity-category of (small) pointed infinity-categories and morphisms that preserve zero objects into the infinity-category of (small) infinity-categories. This adjunction, in turn, leads to the definition of a coherent choice of nullhomotopies on a pointed infinity-category. A coherent choice of nullhomotopies is a non-canonical, coherent choice of "higher zeroes" on a pointed infinity-category, mirroring the obvious definition of higher zeroes on the differential graded nerve of a differential graded category of chain complexes over an additive category. We then show that coherent choices of nullhomotopies give an alternate characterization of fiber sequences in pointed infinity-categories, generalizing the 1-categorical definition of kernels in terms of morphisms that compose to zero.

papers.title: The Arc Threshold of the Two-Row Ising Torus: Exact Factorization, an Algebraic Critical Coupling, Uniformity in the Circumference, and the Rate of Convergence
papers.abstract: The Lee-Yang circle theorem places every zero of a ferromagnetic Ising partition polynomial on the unit circle. The arc condition, that every zero lie in the closed left half-plane, turns the circle theorem into a product formula for the characteristic function of the occupation count and makes it usable for local limit theorems. For the two-row periodic Ising torus we give the exact reflection factorization of the row transfer matrix, reduce the crossing at zeta = i to a real cubic, and identify the critical coupling a_c* = 0.8637850566870... as the unique root in (0,1) of an explicit octic. We prove that every a > a_c* satisfies the arc condition simultaneously for all circumferences, that no smaller coupling does, and that the finite thresholds approach a_c* at the rate C/n^2 with an explicit algebraic constant C. The factorization and the 2x2 threshold are formalized in Lean 4 against Mathlib; the zeta = i reduction, uniformity and rate are analysis-level.

papers.title: Categorical and Floer-theoretic entropies: comparison and counting conjugacy classes in symplectic mapping class groups
papers.abstract: Let $W$ be a Weinstein manifold and let $f: W \to W$ be a compactly supported symplectic automorphism. Using Floer theories, one can define two different entropies of $f$, called "Floer-theoretic" entropy and "categorical" entropy. The current article compares these two entropies and show that the former bounds the latter from below. As an application of the comparison, using that these entropies are invariants up to the conjugate relation, we count conjugacy classes in symplectic mapping classes. Especially, we show an exponential abundance of conjugacy classes that are smoothly isotopic to the identity, when $W$ is a Weinstein manifold of dimension $4n \geq 6$, satisfying a local condition.

papers.title: Biharmonic submanifolds in nonpositive space forms
papers.abstract: We prove that there are no proper biharmonic submanifolds with parallel normalized mean curvature vector field in a nonpositive space form, in arbitrary dimension and codimension. We also prove that every biharmonic surface with flat normal bundle in a four-dimensional nonpositive space form is minimal. These results provide substantial support for Chen's conjecture and the generalized Chen's conjecture for hyperbolic space in higher codimensions.

papers.title: Nonparametric GARCH: An Iterated Neural Estimator
papers.abstract: We study nonparametric estimation and forecasting for GARCH-type processes and propose an iterated neural estimator that alternates between estimating the recursion map and updating the unobserved conditional variances. Under mild conditions, we establish finite-sample bounds for the time-averaged in-sample variance-path error and show that the estimator is minimax rate-optimal up to logarithmic factors. Under stationarity and mixing conditions, we establish the same rate for recursion-map estimation and derive finite-sample bounds for out-of-sample variance forecasts and expected excess Gaussian quasi-likelihood (QLIKE) loss. The convergence rates depend on the true lag orders and remain unchanged when the fitted orders are overspecified. Simulation studies illustrate the effectiveness of our estimators under nonlinear and time-varying volatility dynamics. Real-data applications suggest that our neural methods perform competitively and can incorporate option-price and high-frequency information.

papers.title: A Bubble Compactification of KSBA Moduli Space of Surfaces of General Type
papers.abstract: We construct a bubble-tree enhancement of the KSBA moduli space of surfaces of general type using index-one-cover Deligne--Mumford stacks. The construction is inspired by bubbling phenomena for Kähler--Einstein metrics. Non-klt semi-log-canonical singularities are replaced by admissible simple-normal-crossing configurations: the cusp and degenerate-cusp components are rational, while the simple-elliptic case also contains elliptic ruled components. A key feature is that the construction avoids lci covers. We construct the moduli stack of polarized bubble-tree index-one-cover Deligne-Mumford stacks. The stack is in general not separated, and we construct its underlying separated algebraic space. We also construct the moduli stack of bubble-tree index-one-cover Deligne-Mumford stacks with labeled sections that record algebraic bubbling centers and compare it with the pointed metric bubble tree. The labeled sections determine a numerical class whose stability proves the separatedness of the moduli stack. We establish a perfect obstruction theory and a virtual fundamental class on the bubble-tree moduli stacks. This provides a novel and geometric pathway to prove the existence of a virtual fundamental class on the original KSBA moduli space, thus offering a new approach to a conjecture of Donaldson. We expect that parts of the construction extend to higher dimensions.

papers.title: On the Role of Geometry in Solving Variational Inequalities
papers.abstract: The geometry of constraints in variational inequalities (VIs) plays a central role in applications ranging from resource allocation and equilibrium computation to constrained optimization. Yet, its effect on computational complexity has received surprisingly little attention beyond special cases. We examine this question when the constraint set is an $\ell_p$ ball. This family of problems encompasses two of the most extensively studied classes of problems in algorithmic game theory: symmetric bimatrix games for $p = 1$ and multi-player polymatrix games for $p = \infty$. Both of these problems are known to be PPAD-complete even for affine operators. We establish a comprehensive complexity landscape for VIs over $\ell_p$ balls across the full range $p\in[1,\infty]$. First, for any $p\neq 2$, we show that finding an inverse-polynomial approximate VI solution is PPAD-complete even for affine operators. In contrast, for $p=2$, we give a polynomial-time algorithm for affine VIs, extending a classic result of Ye (1992) beyond symmetric operators. On the other hand, once the operator becomes quadratic, we establish PPAD-completeness even at inverse polynomial precision. From a technical standpoint, we develop a new toolkit for exploiting the geometry of the constraint set and the structure of the operator to characterize the complexity of equilibrium and optimization problems, which is of independent interest.

papers.title: Admissible extremal rays and the anticanonical minimal model program
papers.abstract: We develop an anticanonical minimal model program for projective $\mathbb{Q}$-factorial klt pairs $(X,Δ)$ such that $-(K_{X}+Δ)$ is pseudoeffective. We first prove the cone and contraction theorems for potentially klt triples and establish the existence of flips for such triples. Using these results, we introduce the notion of admissible extremal rays and show that $(K_{X}+Δ)$-positive admissible extremal rays are precisely the rays that are to be contracted by $-(K_{X}+Δ)$-MMP. The elementary MMP steps associated to such admissible rays preserve klt singularities. For potentially klt pairs $(X,Δ)$ with $\mathbb{Q}$-divisors $Δ$, we prove that every $(K_{X}+Δ)$-positive extremal ray is admissible and obtain a cone theorem for the $(K_{X}+Δ)$-positive part of the Mori cone. Assuming termination of the anticanonical minimal model program, we establish a dichotomy: potentially klt pairs admit anticanonical minimal models, whereas non-potentially klt pairs admit non-admissible models.

papers.title: Infinite-Horizon Stochastic Recursive Differential Games with Jumps: Nonautonomous Coefficients and Nonzero Terminal Values
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate a class of decoupled infinite-horizon forward--backward stochastic differential equations (FBSDEs) with time-dependent coefficients and jumps. Under suitable time-integrability conditions on the coefficient growth and stochastic Lipschitz moduli, we establish an $L^p$ theory ($p\ge 2$) for these systems, including well-posedness, moment estimates, conditional stability, and tail estimates, without imposing dissipativity of the forward dynamics or monotonicity of the backward generator in its value variable. In particular, the forward state converges in $L^p$ and almost surely to a limiting random variable $X_\infty$, while the backward solution converges to the generally nonzero terminal value $Φ(X_\infty)$. Within this framework, we study infinite-horizon two-player zero-sum stochastic recursive differential games. We prove that the lower and upper value functions are deterministic and establish the dynamic programming principle (DPP) using backward stochastic semigroups and nonanticipative strategies. Both value functions converge locally uniformly to $Φ$ as the initial time tends to infinity and are characterized as viscosity solutions of the corresponding non-autonomous, nonlocal Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman--Isaacs (HJBI) equations. Under an additional integrable Lyapunov-barrier condition, we establish a comparison principle for continuous viscosity subsolutions and supersolutions of uniform linear growth, provided that at least one is uniformly Lipschitz in space. This yields uniqueness for both HJBI equations in the linear-growth class. Finally, we establish a weaker, contact-wise Isaacs criterion ensuring that the lower and upper value functions coincide and hence that the game has a value.

papers.title: Maps from the Dbar-data to the derivative NLS potentials
papers.abstract: We develop a decomposition technique to investigate maps from the Dbar data to the derivative NLS potentials. We define a new integral operator which is equivalent to a modified Dbar problem relevant to the derivative NLS spectral problem, including the Kaup-Newell spectral problem, the Chen-Lee-Liu spectral problem and the Gerdjikov-Ivanov spectral problem. The well-posedness for the integral operator with the kernel $\mathrm{e}^{ik^2xσ_3}$ is discussed via the decomposition technique. Under different constraint conditions, the derivative NLS potentials are reconstructed via the Dbar data. We discuss the symmetry condition of the Dbar data as well as the compatibility of the derivative NLS spectral problem with the modified Dbar problem. We show that the maps from the Dbar data to the derivative NLS potentials are Lipschitz continuous.

papers.title: An $L^{5/6}$ bound for the periodic Kuramoto-Sivashinsky equation
papers.abstract: We consider the Kuramoto-Sivashinsky equation $u_t+uu_x+u_{xx}+u_{xxxx}=0$ with $L$-periodic boundary conditions and zero spatial mean. We prove that every smooth solution satisfies $\|u(t)\|_{L^2}\leq CL^{5/6}+CL^{3/2}/t$ for $t>0$, where $C$ is a universal constant. In particular, $\|u(t)\|_{L^2}\leq CL^{5/6}$ for all $t\geq L^{2/3}$, independently of the initial norm.

papers.title: Feynman Propagators on Exponentially Decaying Perturbations of Stationary Spacetimes with Compact Cauchy Surface
papers.abstract: In this paper, we construct Feynman propagators on exponentially decaying perturbations of stationary spacetime with compact Cauchy surface. The propagators are defined as parametrices of the wave operator on exponentially weighted Sobolev spaces defined by complex contours $Γ$. We then apply this theory to the computation of indexes of Dirac operators using a continuous Wick-like rotation to relate it to the Riemannian case.

papers.title: Overdetermined boundary problems for maximal graphs
papers.abstract: We study overdetermined boundary problems for the maximal surface equation with zero Dirichlet data and constant nonzero Neumann data . For the exterior of a bounded domain with connected boundary in $\mathbb{R}^n$, $n\geq2$, we prove that such domain must be the complement of a ball and the solution is radial. In dimension two, we also show that a positive solution on a domain bounded by a properly embedded noncompact connected curve forces the domain to be a half-plane and the solution to be affine. The proofs combine the divergence structure of the equation with the induced geometry of maximal graphs.

papers.title: Schrodinger group along the horocycles and Egorov's theorem on compact hyperbolic surfaces
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study Egorov's theorem for Laplacian eigenfunctions on compact hyperbolic surfaces in Zelditch's quantization. In this quantization, the remainder in Egorov's theorem for eigenfunctions is given explicitly by the second derivatives of the symbols along the weak stable foliation of the geodesic flow. Forward in time, we show that Egorov's theorem for eigenfunctions is valid to all logarithmic times, far beyond the Ehrenfest time T_E=|log h|/2, where h going to 0 is the semiclassical parameter. Backward in time, we introduce the Schrodinger group along the stable horocycles, which absorbs the exponentially growing part of the remainder. We show that Egorov's theorem for eigenfunctions is valid up to -T_E+T_h for any Th going to infinity with 0<=T_h<=T_E. Moreover, the limit of the remainder in Egorov's theorem at the Ehrenfest time -T_E is exactly the difference between the semiclassical measure and the Liouville measure, tested against the symbols propagated by the Schrodinger group. Consequently, Egorov's theorem for a sequence of eigenfunctions holds at -T_E (and in fact, at -T_E-T for any fixed T in R if and only if the sequence tends to be equidistributed in the phase space. Thus, the quantum unique ergodicity (QUE) conjecture is equivalent to this Egorov property holding for every eigenbasis. Furthermore, QUE holds with a polynomial rate if and only if Egorov's theorem holds at -T_E with a polynomial remainder. In this case, Egorov's theorem holds beyond -T_E with a polynomial remainder, and the stronger the rate is in QUE, the longer the time is in Egorov's theorem.

papers.title: Global vector fields and the automorphism group of regular semisimple Hessenberg varieties
papers.abstract: For a connected regular semisimple Hessenberg variety other than the full flag variety, we prove that the identity component of its automorphism group is an algebraic torus. The argument uses equivariant local coordinates and weight-homogeneous coefficient functions of vector fields.

papers.title: Algorithmic Non-dimensionalisation of Polynomial Dynamical Systems with CRNNondim
papers.abstract: Although non-dimensionalisation is a fundamental step in modelling, it is rarely obvious, especially for large dynamical systems, how to systematically construct optimal non-dimensionalisations. In this work, we develop a general mathematical framework for non-dimensionalising polynomial ODEs by interpreting them as chemical reaction networks (CRNs) and characterise the space of admissible scalings. Within this viewpoint, admissible scalings of time and species are encoded by Laurent monomials, and we derive exact formulae for the minimal number of multiplicative dimensionless parameters required by the reaction-channel coefficients and by the full initial value problem, together with characterisations of the scale assignments that attain structural lower bounds. These counts are expressed in terms of structural properties of the underlying CRN, and we show that the full initial value problem requires no more parameters than the corresponding Buckingham count. These results lead to constructive algorithms which we analyse rigorously and implement in the open-source Python package CRNNondim, available at https://github.com/georgio-hawi/crnnondim . Given a polynomial system or CRN, CRNNondim determines species and time scalings that bring variables as close to unity as possible while minimising the number of free parameters, and among the admissible scalings it chooses free parameters that result in the corresponding dimensionless system being sparse and simple. We apply CRNNondim to numerous well-known biological and biochemical models, yielding simpler dimensionless systems with fewer free parameters, and interpreting the parameters that govern their dynamics.

papers.title: D-equivalence conjecture for hyperkähler varieties of generalized Kummer type
papers.abstract: We show that birationally equivalent hyperkähler varieties of generalized Kummer type are derived equivalent, confirming the D-equivalence conjecture in this case. Combined with recent results of other authors, this settles the conjecture for all known deformation types of hyperkähler varieties. The kernel is built from an equivariant Fourier-Mukai kernel on the sum-zero loci of powers of an abelian surface. We deform it along diagonal twistor paths, using the hyperholomorphic endomorphism algebra. Comparing wall hyperplanes gives a common twisted derived category for two adjacent birational models, and a finite sequence of wall crossings then gives the equivalence.

papers.title: Improving the performance of regularized Stokeslet simulations using Rosenbrock time integration methods
papers.abstract: The method of regularized Stokeslets (MRS) is widely used to model fluid-structure interactions of microscopic bodies in viscous environments. Specifically, MRS computes the fluid velocity generated by regularized forces distributed on an immersed body, which in turn defines a system of ordinary differential equations with which to evolve the body so that the no-slip condition is enforced. To accurately model material properties such as elasticity and bending rigidity, the resulting ODE system is often stiff and, therefore, computationally expensive to solve with explicit time-integration methods. Here we demonstrate the potential of linearly implicit Rosenbrock (ROS) time integration methods to greatly reduce the computational time required to solve such ODE systems. We focus on the classic model problem of the swimming of a flexible filament driven by preferred curvature forcing. Our findings indicate that, compared to previous MRS simulations, the increased stability of ROS methods allows for speed-ups between twenty and two thousand times over explicit Runge-Kutta (ERK) methods. Moreover, we present approximate scaling laws for this speedup as a function of the key model parameters (bending rigidity and slenderness) at the root of numerical stiffness. Lastly, beyond the basic ROS approach, we discuss several additional strategies that further improve performance.

papers.title: Anti-distinguishability of quantum channels
papers.abstract: We study single-query perfect anti-distinguishability/exclusion tasks of finite quantum channel ensembles, primarily using associated Choi operators and process POVMs. Weak perfect anti-distinguishability requires each measurement outcome to exclude an ensemble candidate with certainty, whereas the strong form additionally requires every candidate to have an exclusion outcome occurring with non-zero probability. For pairs of channels, both coincide with perfect distinguishability, whereas larger ensembles exhibit separations. We derive Choi-operator-support-based obstructions: weak exclusion requires at least two rank-deficient Choi operators, while strong exclusion requires the support of every candidate Choi operator to be strictly contained in the joint Choi support. The common Choi support must also lie in the kernel of the PPOVM normalisation. For commuting Choi operators, this condition is sufficient for weak exclusion when the normalisation also commutes with them. Conversely, a nonzero admixture of the same noise channel into every candidate precludes weak exclusion for any probe. We apply these results to measure-and-prepare, state-space contraction, Pauli, and replacer channels. In particular, the full permutation-channel ensemble of an unlabeled POVM is strongly anti-distinguishable exactly when some POVM effect is rank-deficient, while replacer-channel exclusion reduces to state exclusion. A Choi-commuting ensemble exhibits strong exclusion with an unassisted probe although no positive-definite PPOVM normalisation permits even weak exclusion. In contrast, commuting qubit phase gates, whose Choi operators need not commute, admit exact convex-hull criteria for weak and strong exclusion, both attainable without assistance.

papers.title: Universal bounds for decompositions of PL manifolds
papers.abstract: The geometric dimension of a nonempty compact PL manifold $N$ is the smallest nonnegative integer $d$ for which $N$ admits a handle decomposition with all handles of index at most $d$. A PL filling of a compact PL manifold is a decomposition into compact codimension $0$ PL submanifolds, called sectors, with pairwise disjoint interiors and intersections described by standard local models. We advance Singhof's program of simplifying the sectors of a filling and their intersections. Specifically, for integers $m, \ell\ge 1$ and nonnegative integers $a_1\le\cdots\le a_\ell$, we prove that every closed PL $m$-manifold admits a filling into $\ell$ sectors whose nonempty $r$-fold intersections have geometric dimension at most $a_r$ for each $1\le r\le \ell$ if and only if \[ a_{λ_1}+\cdots+a_{λ_q}\ge m-\ell+1 \] for every partition $λ_1+\cdots+λ_q=\ell$ into positive integers. Under the same inequalities, any prescribed $\ell$-sector filling of the boundary of a compact PL $m$-manifold extends to a filling with the corresponding relative handle index bounds. Necessity follows from the cup-product obstructions of Courte, Moussard, Ren, and Zhou. To prove sufficiency, we develop compatible handle trades that simplify intersections in increasing order of depth. For nondecreasing tuples of nonnegative integers, our theorem resolves the PL classification problem posed by Courte, Moussard, Ren, and Zhou. In particular, we obtain the bound $(2,2,4)$ for $3$-sector fillings in dimension $6$ and improve the $5$-sector bound $(1,2,3,3,4)$ of Rubinstein and Tillmann to $(1,2,2,3,4)$ in dimension $8$.

papers.title: On nearly Lefschetz fibrations and spinal open books
papers.abstract: We survey the recent development of spinal open books and nearly Lefschetz fibrations. The focus is on explaining past and new results regarding the detection of symplectic fillability and classification of symplectic fillings of contact 3-manifolds in light of the new machinery. We give many examples and a list of open questions. This can be considered as an additional chapter to the lecture notes by Ozbacgi and Wendl.

papers.title: Time to AC-t: When AC-transmission changes capacity expansion planning
papers.abstract: Capacity expansion models often dramatically simplify the physics of how power flows through a transmission network in order to preserve computational tractability. However, with the rapid growth of electrification, large loads, renewables, and storage, increased realism in planning future grids is imperative. We extend the open-source capacity expansion model GenX with AC optimal power flow physics, and analyze generation, storage, and transmission investment decisions for 20-zone, hourly models of Germany and Texas. We compare our results against those using two common approximations, the transport model and DC optimal power flow. We find that total costs and emissions largely agree across all formulations. However, we find substantial differences in outputs related to transmission, generation siting, storage, and reactive-power support between the approximate formulations and the true AC physics formulation. We identify where AC physics changes planning decisions and discuss how to potentially capture these effects without the full computational cost.

papers.title: Runtime Compilation for Quantum Circuits with PQF-Enabled $R_z$ Synthesis
papers.abstract: In Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computing (FTQC) using surface codes, reducing $T$-count is critical for efficient computation due to the high cost of $T$-state distillation. Probabilistic Quantum Circuit with Fallback (PQF) synthesis significantly lowers $T$-counts compared to standard protocols like Gridsynth, but introduces high circuit dynamism through extra gates inserted at runtime. This dynamism invalidates static compile-time routing, as these new $T$ gates require dynamic lattice surgery routing to establish non-intersecting ancilla paths to $T$-state factories while minimizing total execution time. To address this, we introduce $\text{R}^2$-PQF, a Runtime Routing protocol for PQF-synthesized quantum circuits. $\text{R}^2$-PQF dynamically routes gates layer-by-layer, computing paths during the execution of the previous logical timestep. To satisfy the strict computational window of $\sim t_{lattice\_surgery} + t_{reaction}$ and non-intersectionality constraints, we implement a Wavefront Breadth-First Search (W-BFS) and synthesise it on a 500MHz FPGA and 2 GHz ASIC. For a clock cycle of 2GHz, we achieve a median logical time-step of $1.51 μs$ for a 300 qubit Ising Hamiltonian circuit, demonstrating that $\text{R}^2$-PQF successfully resolves the vast majority of paths (with rare exceptions) within the execution window and enables the $T$-count benefits of PQF without latency penalties. Compared to a baseline stalling-based solution (the only no-runtime-recomputation solution), $\text{R}^2$-PQF speeds up circuit execution by $1.34\times$ on average and up to $1.76 \times$.

papers.title: Bounds for Orthogonal Expansion Coefficients via Weighted Primitives
papers.abstract: For trigonometric and polynomial orthogonal expansions, we present coefficient bounds with an explicit numerator determined by the total variation of the function and the largest cumulative signed area of the weighted basis element. This area, denoted by $M_n$, is the sharp constant in the corresponding weighted integral estimate. We calculate or bound $M_n$ for several classical systems, thereby obtaining quantitative inequalities beyond an asymptotic statement of coefficient decay. Integration between consecutive zeros gives a geometric interpretation of the estimate. The comparison includes Chebyshev polynomials of the first three kinds, Legendre, Jacobi, Gegenbauer, and ordinary Laguerre polynomials, with normalization and boundary conditions stated explicitly. Classical estimates and their elementary consequences are organized as Fourier analysis in inequalities. In the controlled distortion application, ideal curves have selected coefficients absent, and restrictions on the variation, corridor width, and number of extrema of admissible departures give explicit guarantees for those coefficients.

papers.title: Adaptive data-driven reduced-order models for reciprocal MIMO port-Hamiltonian dynamical systems
papers.abstract: Port-Hamiltonian (pH) systems provide a general framework for modeling a broad class of physical dynamical systems, including systems with dissipation. Constructing accurate and robust data-driven reduced-order models for general pH systems is challenging. In this work, we focus on an important subclass of pH systems satisfying reciprocity, a property arising naturally in a variety of models. Rather than seeking to preserve the full pH structure, we exploit the additional symmetry provided by reciprocity to develop an efficient data-driven reduced-order modeling approach. We show that every minimal realization of a reciprocal system is self-adjoint with respect to a generally indefinite inner product and can, up to a similarity transformation preserving the pH structure, be represented in a Krein space with a signature inner product. This observation motivates a Galerkin projection onto a tangential rational Krylov subspace with respect to the corresponding indefinite inner product. Although the resulting projection involves full-order state solutions and the unknown inner product, we show that its reduced mass and stiffness matrices can be constructed directly from transfer-function data through a Loewner formulation. We then propose a greedy data-driven procedure that adaptively selects both interpolation frequencies and tangential directions. At every iteration, the frequency is chosen according to the largest transfer-function approximation error, while the tangential direction is selected from a dominant singular direction of the corresponding matrix-valued residual. Numerical experiments for wave propagation in lossy media demonstrate improved approximation efficiency compared with block adaptive interpolation. We further apply the method to spectral mass gauging of a three-dimensional propellant tank to provide an accurate estimate of the tank volume through Weyl's law.

papers.title: Minimax signal detection in regression under differential privacy
papers.abstract: We establish minimax separation rates across sparsity levels for regression signal detection under $(ε, δ)$-central differential privacy, considering linear regression with an unknown error distribution and generalised linear models (GLMs) with an unknown intercept. Without sparsity restrictions, the separation rates for linear regression and GLMs with binary responses match the private Gaussian mean testing rate up to polylogarithmic factors. For GLMs with more than two possible response outcomes, additional information in the marginal response distribution permits faster detection of sufficiently small signals when the dimension exceeds the sample size $n$. Our upper bounds are based on a reduction to private mean testing, tests of dependence between the response and sparse covariate projections, and a response-only test that is adjusted for the unknown intercept. The resulting procedure adapts to unknown sparsity and matches our lower bounds up to polylogarithmic factors. We also construct polynomial-time tests that attain these rates when $ε\gtrsim n^{-1/2}$, and compare their numerical performance with existing private procedures.

papers.title: StreamLTT: Risk Certification for Policy Selection under Stream Dependence
papers.abstract: Learn-then-Test (LTT) provides a general framework for certifying deployment policies against a prescribed risk target, but its standard formulation targets a fixed population risk estimated from calibration losses. In sequential deployment, losses may instead be dependent and nonstationary, so the risk of a fixed policy can evolve with the observed history. We introduce StreamLTT, which replaces this fixed population risk with average predictable risk, defined by conditioning each decision's loss on the information available before its outcome is revealed. Conditional centering turns empirical deviations from this target into a martingale sum, enabling both a test that adapts to predictable variance and a finite-sample Hoeffding alternative. Combined with family-wise error rate control, StreamLTT yields a simultaneously certified policy region that supports subsequent deployment selection. Across seven forecasting datasets and seven deployment risks, StreamLTT places the certified frontier substantially closer to the prescribed risk target than IID, robust-variance, block-bootstrap, and concentration-based alternatives, while empirical family-wise error closely follows the prescribed level. A finite-sample ablation further shows that the predictable-risk formulation drives the tighter risk frontier, while adaptation to predictable variance makes more effective use of the available family-wise error budget. StreamLTT therefore extends risk-certified policy selection to dependent deployment streams by addressing both what risk should be certified and how it should be tested.

papers.title: Revisiting the Upper Bild of Quaternionic Numerical Ranges
papers.abstract: The upper bild of the quaternionic numerical range provides a convex representative of the generally nonconvex quaternionic numerical range. Although its convexity is known, the geometry of the upper bild is difficult to describe explicitly, even for 2-by-2 quaternionic matrices. In this paper, we revisit the upper bild of quaternionic numerical ranges from both algebraic and geometric viewpoints. We first point out gaps in Kumar's proof. We then investigate several special classes of 2-by-2 quaternionic matrices and describe their shapes and boundary structures in the closed upper complex half-plane directly in terms of the standard eigenvalues and the off-diagonal entry of the Schur form. For the general 2-by-2 case, we use a different canonical form. Following So and Thompson, we prove the concavity of the upper-boundary function through the associated complex representation. For the lower boundary, we obtain a distance-to-a-disk representation and use convex optimization to prove its convexity. We also treat the degenerate cases. Together with the connectedness of the vertical sections, these results give an alternative proof of the convexity of the upper bild for arbitrary quaternionic matrices.

papers.title: A Review of Max-Pressure Traffic Signal Control Algorithms: State of the Art and Research Opportunities
papers.abstract: Max-Pressure (MP) has emerged as a widely studied decentralized traffic signal control framework, thanks to its desirable theoretical properties and strong control performance. Early research on MP focused on improving control performance by exploring different variables of the traffic state for the definition of pressure. Subsequent studies expanded MP to incorporate the complexity of real-world transportation systems and emerging technologies. This paper provides a comprehensive review of these developments. The review first introduces the theoretical foundations of MP and examines early developments in movement weight definition. It then synthesizes major extensions for multimodal and multiscale network control, followed by recent developments in connected and automated vehicle (CAV) environments and the integration of MP with artificial intelligence (AI) and data-driven methods. Beyond summarizing existing approaches, this review examines their underlying assumptions, data requirements, implementation considerations, and practical limitations. Based on this comprehensive review, key research gaps and future directions are identified, including remaining limitations in the theoretical foundations of MP and the underexplored integration of autonomous vehicle control with the MP framework. Overall, this review provides a structured perspective on the evolution and current state of MP control and highlights opportunities for developing more proactive, robust, and practically deployable MP-based traffic control methods.

papers.title: Fixed-grid schemes for fractional moving-boundary problems
papers.abstract: The Landau transformation xi = x/s(t) is the usual way to hold a moving boundary in place. It fails for fractional time derivatives because they have no chain rule: the transformed operator gains a nonlocal integral with a closed form only for self-similar fronts. We develop a sharp-interface finite-difference scheme for the conservation-consistent memory-flux fractional Stefan problem on a fixed grid, storing the memory limit h(x) = s^-1(x) as the time each node melts. The front is advanced using an integrated energy balance, with the singular source timed to the sub-step crossing instant. Against a known self-similar solution, the front constant is accurate to 0.02 to 0.11%, whereas competing formulations differ by 17 to 27% at alpha = 0.6. A remaining positivity violation follows from dt/t0 ~ s0^(1 - 2/alpha) and disappears on a front-locked time grid. We also derive two exact solutions with non-power-law fronts: a source-dominated solution and a Mittag-Leffler traveling wave, and verify the scheme against both. Neural-network solvers for moving boundaries are often trained in normalized coordinates; for alpha < 1, this silently changes the problem, while the change vanishes at alpha = 1, where checks are commonly performed. In the classical limit, our scheme is more accurate in 12 ms than a reimplemented moving-boundary network in 177 s.

papers.title: Hochschild cohomology of Temperley--Lieb algebras: a Kauffman diagram perspective
papers.abstract: We describe Hochschild cohomology of Temperley--Lieb algebras by explicit minimal-resolution coordinates and multilinear operations on Kauffman diagrams. For each doubled-line basic algebra, a finite four-term bimodule complex is verified by a signed-shuffle comparison and an augmented contracting homotopy. We compute cocycles and coboundaries and recover the known cup product and Gerstenhaber bracket in explicit representatives. Over $\mathbb C$, at nonzero root-of-unity loop parameters, we construct a tower-compatible derivation and the marked-circle two-cocycle. Their classes are nonzero on every nonsemisimple block; their cup products therefore represent all positive classes over the centre. Relative full twists give a compact expression for the derivation. Worked planar diagrams distinguish the cup product from insertion and strict cochain equalities from equalities of classes. A finite-lattice section interprets the marked-circle operation as loop-weight response, derives its planar Potts normalization, and exhibits a six-vertex realization. It also shows why passing to a deformable spin representation may annihilate the class with different coefficients. No thermodynamic conclusion is claimed, and the even-strand zero-parameter family remains separate.

papers.title: Automatic partition identities
papers.abstract: We encode certain sets of partitions by regular languages of boundary words, so that their generating functions become rational series in the quantum plane $RU=qUR$. An equality between two partition counts is certified by writing the difference of their series as $(1-U)a+b(1-R)$, with $a,b$ converging $q$-adically. We show that $a,b$ may be chosen as solutions of finite holonomic systems of $q$-difference equations computed from the automata, and describe finite certificates of their convergence, together with bounded searches for such certificates; the searches need not succeed, but a false identity is always detected. As an application, we prove the three-row, level-two case of Primc's conjecture, which equates counts of coloured partitions subject to local multiplicity conditions with counts of coloured partitions whose parts lie in prescribed residue classes modulo eight.

papers.title: Some instances of modularity for residually reducible representations in the mixed case
papers.abstract: Let $F$ be a totally real field, abelian over $\Q$, in which an odd prime $p$ splits completely, and let $ρ:G_F\to\GL_2(\overline\Q_p)$ be an odd irreducible representation which is de Rham with distinct Hodge--Tate weights at the places above $p$ and whose residual representation is reducible.
